items.title: Welcome to the exaMPM online documentation!
items.text:
exascale Material Point Method Large-deformation continuum mechanics (landslides, impacts, soil-structure interaction) with the Material Point Method, written as an application of the onika + exaNBody HPC frameworks.

Prototype

exaMPM is a young prototype. It reproduces the 3D MPM solver of mpmxdem on exaNBody data structures, runs on CPU (OpenMP) and GPU (CUDA), and does not support MPI runs yet. Interfaces and YAML keys may still change.

  • Features

    • Material Point Method, modified Lagrangian scheme
    • Mohr-Coulomb and Hooke constitutive models
    • Rigid obstacles: spheres, planes, cylinders, biplanar slopes
    • Geometry from Blender (coordinate files, STL)
    • OpenMP and GPU (CUDA) kernels from one source

    All features

  • Access to the code

    • GitHub repository to access the code and fork it.
    • Open an issue to report bugs.
    • Create a pull request to propose developments.

  • Get started

    • Build & Install onika, exaNBody, mpmxdem and exaMPM
    • Write a first input deck with the Beginner Guide
    • Run the ported mpmxdem Tutorials

  • Open Source, GPL v3

    exaMPM links the mpmxdem library, distributed under the GNU GPL v3: an exaMPM build is therefore GPL v3.

items.title: Project summary
items.text: exaMPM (exascale Material Point Method) is a prototype of Material Point Method code built on the onika and exaNBody HPC frameworks, in the Collab4exaNBody collaboration, alongside exaStamp and exaDEM. It reproduces the 3D MPM solver of mpmxdem on exaNBody data structures, with kernels that run with OpenMP and on GPUs.

items.title: Beginner Guide
items.text:
New to exaMPM? This guide goes from the core concepts to a complete, runnable input deck.

  • Getting Started — how a simulation is a graph of operators, how configuration files are combined, and the YAML syntax used to write them
  • Simulation Starter Pack — a step-by-step walkthrough of a minimal MPM simulation: global settings, domain and grid, material points, obstacles, constitutive model, time scheme and outputs

For the full reference material, see the User Guide tab.

items.title: Getting Started
items.text:
exaMPM has no main() that you edit and no fixed input format: a simulation is a graph of operators described in YAML. These pages explain the three ideas you need before writing a deck:

  • Building blocks — operators, slots and batches
  • Configuration files — the default configuration and how a deck overrides it
  • YAML basics — the YAML syntax and the onika extensions used in .msp files

items.title: Operators
items.text:
An operator is a small C++ component that does one thing: create material points, transfer the mass to the grid, compute contact forces, write a file... Each operator has typed slots: its inputs and outputs.

$ exaMPM --help set_mp_grid
Operator    : set_mp_grid

Description : Fills a box with cubic material points of side 'size', at rest and stress free, like mpmxdem's
set_MP_grid command. Also sets the previous position to the current one (mpmxdem: MPMbox::init).
Slots       :
  density
    flow IN
    type double
    desc mass density (mpmxdem: mass_density)
  group
    flow IN
    type long
    desc MP group, stored in the 'type' field (mpmxdem: groupNb)
  lower
    flow IN
    type math::Vec3d
    desc lower corner of the box (x0, y0, z0)
  ...

Slots are connected by name: when parameters outputs gravity, every later operator with a gravity input reads that value. You never wire operators by hand.

items.title: Batches
items.text:
A YAML list of operators is a batch: the operators run in order. A batch can be given a name and used as an operator itself:

mpm_init:          # a batch named mpm_init ...
  - init_nodes     # ... made of two operators
  - update_mp_cells

init_epilog: mpm_init   # ... used where the hook init_epilog is called

Batches can also loop (loop: true with a condition slot) or run conditionally (condition: with a boolean slot). The MPM time loop mpm_compute_loop is such a batch.

items.title: Setting slot values
items.text:
A slot value is given in YAML under the operator name:

- set_mp_grid: { group: 0, density: 2000., lower: [ 3.5, 0.5, 0.3 ], upper: [ 3.9, 1.0, 2.7 ], size: 0.02 }

Values not given keep the default of the operator (shown by --help). Slots marked REQUIRED must be set, or be produced by an earlier operator.

Units

exaMPM decks currently give SI values without units (m, kg, s, Pa). Angles of the constitutive models are in radians, rotation angles of move_mp and LeftBiplanar in degrees.

items.title: Configuration files
items.text:
Every run reads, in this order:

  1. data/config/main-config.msp — the default simulation graph, installed with exaMPM;
  2. the files listed under its includes: key, here config_globals.msp (default global values);
  3. your deck, given on the command line.

A later file overrides earlier definitions key by key. The default simulation block runs a fixed sequence of hooks:

simulation:
  name: sim
  body:
    - print_logo_banner
    - hw_device_init      # MPI and GPU initialization
    - init_prolog         # default: global
    - input_data          # nop: domain, material points, obstacles...
    - init_epilog         # nop: MPM decks use mpm_init
    - first_iteration     # nop
    - compute_loop        # nop: MPM decks use mpm_compute_loop
    - simulation_epilog   # nop
    - hw_device_finalize

A deck never edits simulation: it fills the hooks. An MPM deck typically defines input_data and sets

init_epilog: mpm_init
compute_loop: mpm_compute_loop
mpm_constitutive_model:
  - mohr_coulomb: { ... }

The complete default configuration is shown in Default YAML.

items.title: Overriding and appending
items.text:
• key: value replaces the whole block key;
  • inside a map, only the keys you give are replaced (e.g. global: { dt: 1.0e-6 } keeps the other globals);
  • +key: [ ... ] appends operators to the batch key instead of replacing it:
+mpm_log_extra:
  - print_obstacles

items.title: YAML basics
items.text:
.msp files are YAML. The constructs used in exaMPM decks are:

# a comment
global:                        # a map (block)
  dt: 1.0e-5                   # scalar
  simulation_end_iteration: 49999

input_data:                    # a list (batch of operators)
  - grid_flavor_mpm            # operator without parameters
  - parameters:                # operator with parameters, block style
      gravity: [ 0.0 , -9.81 , 0.0 ]   # a vector
  - set_mp_grid: { group: 0, density: 2000., size: 0.02,      # flow style
                   lower: [ 3.5, 0.5, 0.3 ], upper: [ 3.9, 1.0, 2.7 ] }
  - obstacles:
      obstacles:               # a list of strings
        - "Sphere 0 3.1 1.0 1.4 0.1 free 30000.0 2.0 0.1 0 0"

items.title: onika extensions
items.text:
Syntax Meaning includes: [ file.msp ] read other configuration files first (searched in ONIKA_CONFIG_PATH) +key: [ ... ] append to the batch key instead of replacing it name: other_block the hook name runs the batch other_block rebind: { slot: other } inside a batch, read/write the slot slot under the name other loop: true, condition: slot repeat the batch while the boolean slot is true condition: slot (without loop) run the batch only if the slot is true configuration: runtime options (threads, GPU, logging, profiling, debug)

Debugging a deck

--debug-graph true prints the operator graph actually executed, and --debug-config true the final merged configuration.

items.title: Simulation Starter Pack
items.text:
A minimal MPM deck defines, on top of the default configuration:

global:                  # time step, number of steps, output periods
input_data:              # gravity, domain (= background grid), material points, obstacles, contact laws
init_epilog: mpm_init    # initialize the MPM nodes
compute_loop: mpm_compute_loop      # the MPM time loop
mpm_constitutive_model:  # the constitutive model of each group of material points

The time scheme (mpm_modified_lagrangian) and the outputs already have working defaults, but they are covered too.

The following pages build, block by block, the deck of the sphere impacting a structure tutorial:

  • Global control — time step, end of the run, output periods through global
  • Domain and background grid — the MPM grid through domain
  • Material points — gravity and material points through parameters and set_mp_grid
  • Obstacles and contacts — rigid bodies through obstacles and contact_laws
  • Constitutive model — the material behaviour through mpm_constitutive_model
  • Numerical scheme — the time loop mpm_compute_loop
  • Output data — log, ParaView files
  • Working example — the complete deck

items.title: Global Control
items.text:
The global operator, run by the hook init_prolog, creates the slots shared by the whole simulation. Its default values are defined in data/config/config_globals.msp:

############ some global properties ############
# Default values of the global simulation slots, created by the 'global' operator (run in init_prolog).
# A deck overrides them key by key, e.g. global: { dt: 1.0e-5 , simulation_end_iteration: 49999 }.
# Values are given without units and are taken as SI (m, kg, s).

global:
  dt: 1.0e-5                     # time step (mpmxdem: dt)
  timestep: 0                    # current time step
  physical_time: 0.0             # current time (mpmxdem: t)
  simulation_end_iteration: 0    # last time step: the loop runs timesteps 0 .. simulation_end_iteration
  compute_loop_continue: true
  mpm_vtk_period: 1000           # paraview output period (mpmxdem: vtkPeriod)
  mpm_prox_period: 100           # proximity check period (mpmxdem: proxPeriod)
  mpm_log_period: 1000           # obstacle log period
Parameters' description Parameter Description Type Default dt time step (s) float 1.0e-5 timestep current time step int 0 physical_time current time (s) float 0.0 simulation_end_iteration last time step: the loop runs the steps 0 .. simulation_end_iteration int 0 compute_loop_continue loop condition, set to false by the loop itself bool true mpm_vtk_period ParaView output period (steps) int 1000 mpm_prox_period period of the proximity check of the contacts (steps) int 100 mpm_log_period log line period (steps) int 1000

A deck overrides only what it needs:

global:
  dt: 1.0e-5
  simulation_end_iteration: 49999   # 50000 steps = 0.5 s

Time step

MPM with explicit time integration is conditionally stable: dt must stay below the time for an elastic wave to cross one grid element, \(\Delta t < h / c\) with \(c = \sqrt{E/\rho}\) (times a safety factor).

items.title: Domain and Background Grid
items.text:
In exaMPM, the exaNBody domain is the MPM background grid: every exaNBody cell holds exactly one MPM node, at its centre. The cell size is the MPM element size \(h\).

To get nodes at \(x = 0, h, 2h, \dots, n h\) (n elements), the domain has \(n+1\) cells and starts at \(-h/2\):

input_data:
  # MPM grid of 100 x 40 x 55 elements of 0.06 m
  - domain:
      cell_size: 0.06
      grid_dims: [ 101 , 41 , 56 ]                                   # elements + 1
      bounds: [ [ -0.03 , -0.03 , -0.03 ] , [ 6.03 , 2.43 , 3.33 ] ]  # [-h/2, n h + h/2]
      periodic: [ false , false , false ]
      expandable: false
  - grid_flavor_mpm      # selects the exaMPM particle grid (must come before the MPs are created)
  - init_rcb_grid        # allocates the grid of cells
Parameters' description Property Type Description cell_size float MPM element size \(h\) grid_dims [int;3] number of cells = number of elements + 1 along each axis bounds AABB [[xmin,ymin,zmin],[xmax,ymax,zmax]], from \(-h/2\) to \(n h + h/2\) periodic [bool;3] must be false: periodic MPM grids are not supported expandable bool must be false: the grid is fixed

mpmxdem equivalent

new_set_grid nx ny nz h in mpmxdem (n elements of size h along each axis) becomes cell_size: h, grid_dims: [nx+1, ny+1, nz+1] and bounds: [[-h/2,-h/2,-h/2], [nx h + h/2, ny h + h/2, nz h + h/2]].

Material points must stay inside the grid: p2g_mass aborts the run when a material point leaves it, like mpmxdem. See Background Grid for the shape functions and the nodal fields.

items.title: Gravity
items.text:
The parameters operator sets the gravity and the mass tolerance used by the transfer operators:

  - parameters:
      gravity: [ 0.0 , -9.81 , 0.0 ]   # y is the vertical axis in all examples
Parameter Description Default gravity gravity acceleration (m/s²) [0, 0, 0] tolmass nodes lighter than this are ignored in grid-to-particle transfers 1e-6

items.title: Creating material points
items.text:
set_mp_grid fills a box with cubic material points of side size, at rest and stress free:

  - set_mp_grid: { group: 0, density: 2000., lower: [ 3.5 , 0.5 , 0.3 ], upper: [ 3.9 , 1.0 , 2.7 ], size: 0.02 }
Parameter Description Default group material point group, stored in the type field: selects the constitutive model and the contact laws 0 density mass density (kg/m³) required lower, upper corners of the box required size side of the cubic material points: volume size³, mass density × size³ required

Several setters can be chained to build more complex bodies: other boxes, Blender objects or STL meshes (blender_set_mp_grid), rigid motions (move_mp), a new group in a region (blender_modify_mp), and an initial geostatic stress (set_k0_stress). See Material Points.

Material point size

Use 2 to 3 material points per element and direction (here \(h = 0.06\), size = 0.02: 27 MPs per element).

items.title: Obstacles and Contacts
items.text:
Rigid obstacles are created by the obstacles operator from one line per obstacle, with the syntax of mpmxdem's Obstacle command. The first word is the obstacle type, the second its group:

  - obstacles:
      obstacles:
        # Sphere group xc yc zc R driveMode [density vx vy vz vrot]
        - "Sphere 0 3.1 1.0 1.4 0.1 free 30000.0 2.0 0.1 0 0"
        # Plane group x0 y0 z0  x1 y1 z1  x2 y2 z2  x3 y3 z3   (corners, clockwise)
        - "Plane 1 0.0 0.5 0.0 8.0 0.5 0.0 8.0 0.5 4.0 0.0 0.5 4.0"

Here a free sphere of radius 0.1 m and density 30000 kg/m³ is thrown at 2 m/s along x, and a horizontal plane at y = 0.5 m holds the block.

items.title: Contact laws
items.text:
The contact between a material point and an obstacle is a penalty law with friction, whose parameters are given per (material point group, obstacle group) with mpmxdem's set syntax <param> groupMP groupObst value:

  - contact_laws:
      set: [ "mu 0 0 0.3", "kn 0 0 1.0e6", "en2 0 0 0.8", "kt 0 0 0.5e6",     # MPs of group 0 / sphere
             "mu 0 1 1.0", "kn 0 1 1.0e6", "en2 0 1 0.8", "kt 0 1 0.5e6" ]    # MPs of group 0 / plane
Parameter Description kn normal stiffness kt tangential stiffness en2 unloading factor (square of the restitution coefficient): \(f_n = -k_n\,e_n^2\,d_n\) when unloading mu friction coefficient

Warning

A missing (group, group) pair gives a zero law: the material points go through the obstacle.

See Obstacles & Contacts for all obstacle types and the contact law.

items.title: Constitutive Model
items.text:
The hook mpm_constitutive_model is called at each time step to compute the strain increment and update the stress of the material points. It is a batch: list one model per material point group.

mpm_constitutive_model:
  - mohr_coulomb: { group: 0, young: 8.0e6, poisson: 0.42, friction_angle: 0.7, cohesion: 1e4, dilatancy_angle: 0.05 }
Parameter Description Default group material point group using this model, -1 for all -1 young Young modulus (Pa) 200e6 poisson Poisson ratio 0.2 friction_angle friction angle (rad) 0.5 cohesion cohesion (Pa) 0 dilatancy_angle dilatancy angle (rad) 0.3

Two models are available: mohr_coulomb and hooke_elasticity (linear elasticity). A two-material deck looks like:

mpm_constitutive_model:
  - hooke_elasticity: { group: 0, young: 200.0e8, poisson: 0.42 }
  - mohr_coulomb: { group: 1, young: 70.0e6, poisson: 0.42, friction_angle: 0.5, cohesion: 50., dilatancy_angle: 0.05 }

See Constitutive Models.

items.title: Numerical Scheme
items.text:
Two hooks of the default simulation block start the MPM computation:

init_epilog: mpm_init            # allocates the MPM nodes, lists the cells holding MPs
compute_loop: mpm_compute_loop   # the time loop

mpm_compute_loop repeats, until simulation_end_iteration:

mpm_compute_loop:
  loop: true
  condition: compute_loop_continue
  body:
    - mpm_begin_iteration       # outputs, log and proximity check at their periods
    - mpm_modified_lagrangian   # one MPM step
    - next_time_step            # timestep += 1, physical_time += dt
    - mpm_compute_loop_stop     # compute_loop_continue = timestep <= simulation_end_iteration

One step, mpm_modified_lagrangian, is mpmxdem's modified Lagrangian scheme split into operators:

flowchart TD
  A[obstacles_reset / reset_nodes / obstacles_predict] --> B[update_mass, p2g_mass]
  B --> C[p2g_internal_forces]
  C --> D[contact_forces, obstacles_correct, p2g_contact_forces]
  D --> E[grid_momentum_rate]
  E --> F[g2p_velocity, p2g_momentum]
  F --> G[mpm_constitutive_model]
  G --> H[update_volume, g2p_position]

You normally do not change it. See Numerical Scheme for the equations of each operator.

items.title: Output Data
items.text:
By default, mpm_begin_iteration writes, at the first step and then periodically:

Output Period Files log line (screen and file) mpm_log_period ExaMPMOutputDir/log.txt material points (ParaView) mpm_vtk_period mpm_paraview/mpm_<step>.pvtp obstacle surfaces (ParaView) mpm_vtk_period mpm_paraview/obstacles_<step>.vtk

The log line looks like:

     Step     Time               MPs  Act. nodes   Contacts       Mass     Volume    avg. Ec    max |v|    avg. p  Throughput (MP/s)
        0  0.000000e+00         57000           0          0  9.120e+02  4.560e-01  0.000e+00  0.000e+00  0.000e+00  0.0000e+00
      100  1.000000e-03         57000        3280       2280  9.120e+02  4.560e-01  6.427e-07  9.810e-03  1.438e+02  4.0420e+06
      200  2.000000e-03         57000        3280       2280  9.120e+02  4.560e-01  2.231e-06  1.962e-02  5.369e+02  4.0033e+06

(sphere_impacting_structure.msp with --set-global-mpm_log_period 100, 4 threads.) The columns are: number of material points, active nodes (mass above tolmass), active material point-obstacle contacts, total mass and volume, average kinetic energy per material point, maximum velocity, mean pressure \(-\mathrm{tr}(\sigma)/3\), and material point updates per second since the previous line.

Extra outputs are added through hooks:

# also print the position, velocity and force of the free obstacles at each log line
mpm_log_extra: print_obstacles

# also write the MP positions in mpmxdem's mpPos<n>.txt format
mpm_vtk_output: [ mpm_write_paraview, save_mp_pos ]

See Outputs for the fields written and Visualization to open them in ParaView.

items.title: Working Example
items.text:
The complete deck gathers all the blocks of the previous pages. It is example/sphere_impacting_structure/sphere_impacting_structure.msp, the port of mpmxdem's sphereImpactingStructure.sim: a rigid sphere hits a Mohr-Coulomb block lying on a plane.

# mpmxdem mpm/3D/Examples/sphereImpactingStructure.sim: a rigid sphere hits a Mohr-Coulomb block on a plane.
# SI units. Add '--nogpu false' to run on the GPU.

configuration:
  nogpu: true

global:
  dt: 1.0e-5
  simulation_end_iteration: 49999   # 0.5 s

input_data:
  - parameters:
      gravity: [ 0.0 , -9.81 , 0.0 ]
  # MPM grid of 100 x 40 x 55 elements of 0.06 m: one exaNBody cell per node, domain shifted by -h/2
  - domain:
      cell_size: 0.06
      grid_dims: [ 101 , 41 , 56 ]
      bounds: [ [ -0.03 , -0.03 , -0.03 ] , [ 6.03 , 2.43 , 3.33 ] ]
      periodic: [ false , false , false ]
      expandable: false
  - grid_flavor_mpm
  - init_rcb_grid
  - set_mp_grid: { group: 0, density: 2000., lower: [ 3.5 , 0.5 , 0.3 ], upper: [ 3.9 , 1.0 , 2.7 ], size: 0.02 }
  - obstacles:
      obstacles:
        - "Sphere 0 3.1 1.0 1.4 0.1 free 30000.0 2.0 0.1 0 0"
        - "Plane 1 0.0 0.5 0.0 8.0 0.5 0.0 8.0 0.5 4.0 0.0 0.5 4.0"
  - contact_laws:
      set: [ "mu 0 0 0.3", "kn 0 0 1.0e6", "en2 0 0 0.8", "kt 0 0 0.5e6",
             "mu 0 1 1.0", "kn 0 1 1.0e6", "en2 0 1 0.8", "kt 0 1 0.5e6" ]

init_epilog: mpm_init
compute_loop: mpm_compute_loop

mpm_constitutive_model:
  - mohr_coulomb: { group: 0, young: 8.0e6, poisson: 0.42, friction_angle: 0.7, cohesion: 1e4, dilatancy_angle: 0.05 }

Run it in its folder of the build tree (see Running an example):

cd build-exampm/example/sphere_impacting_structure
../exaMPM sphere_impacting_structure.msp --omp_num_threads 8
# or a short test run
../exaMPM sphere_impacting_structure.msp --set-global-simulation_end_iteration 199 --set-global-mpm_vtk_period 100

Then open mpm_paraview/mpm_*.pvtp and mpm_paraview/obstacles_*.vtk in ParaView. The tutorial discusses the results.

items.title: Installation guide
items.text:
exaMPM is written in C++20 and built with CMake under Linux. It depends on four packages, built in this order:

flowchart LR
  yaml[yaml-cpp] --> onika
  onika --> exaNBody
  exaNBody --> exaMPM
  mpmxdem --> exaMPM
  • CMake installation: requirements, then onika, exaNBody, mpmxdem and exaMPM from their sources.
  • Running your simulation: the exaMPM wrapper, command-line options, threads and GPU.

No Spack package yet

Unlike exaStamp, exaMPM has no Spack package for now: use the CMake procedure.

items.title: Installation with CMake
items.text:
The required minimal CMake version is 3.26. The commands below use these environment variables (choose your own paths):

Variable Meaning ONIKA_SRC_DIR / ONIKA_INSTALL_DIR onika source tree / install prefix XNB_SRC_DIR / XNB_INSTALL_DIR exaNBody source tree / install prefix MPMXDEM_SRC_DIR / MPMXDEM_INSTALL_DIR mpmxdem source tree (branch add_cmake) / install prefix EXAMPM_SRC_DIR / EXAMPM_INSTALL_DIR exaMPM source tree / install prefix

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
• CMake ≥ 3.26, a C++20 compiler with OpenMP, MPI and yaml-cpp;
  • git and network access when configuring mpmxdem (it fetches toofus);
  • optional: CUDA, to run the kernels on NVIDIA GPUs.
Ubuntu / Debianyaml-cpp from sources 
sudo apt install cmake g++ libyaml-cpp-dev mpich libmpich-dev

See the exaStamp documentation for a yaml-cpp build with CMake, then add -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=${YAML_CPP_INSTALL_DIR} to the onika command.

items.title: Onika
items.text:
onika is the component-based HPC platform under exaNBody: operators, YAML, OpenMP, CUDA/HIP.

Linux x GCCLinux x GCC x CUDA 
git clone https://github.com/Collab4exaNBody/onika.git ${ONIKA_SRC_DIR}
cmake -S ${ONIKA_SRC_DIR} -B build-onika -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=${ONIKA_INSTALL_DIR} \
      -DONIKA_BUILD_CUDA=OFF
cmake --build build-onika --target install -j10

git clone https://github.com/Collab4exaNBody/onika.git ${ONIKA_SRC_DIR}
cmake -S ${ONIKA_SRC_DIR} -B build-onika -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=${ONIKA_INSTALL_DIR} \
      -DONIKA_BUILD_CUDA=ON \
      -DCMAKE_CUDA_COMPILER=$(which nvcc) \
      -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=${ARCH}
cmake --build build-onika --target install -j10

${ARCH} is the GPU architecture, e.g. 80 for an A100, 89 for an RTX 40xx.

items.title: exaNBody
items.text:
git clone https://github.com/Collab4exaNBody/exaNBody.git ${XNB_SRC_DIR}
source ${ONIKA_INSTALL_DIR}/bin/setup-env.sh
cmake -S ${XNB_SRC_DIR} -B build-exanb -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      -Donika_DIR=${ONIKA_INSTALL_DIR} \
      -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=${XNB_INSTALL_DIR}
cmake --build build-exanb --target install -j10

items.title: mpmxdem
items.text:
exaMPM uses an installed mpmxdem (headers of toofus, PBC3D library, and the reference solver mpmbox3D). Only the 3D part is needed, so the 2D part (which needs OpenGL/GLUT) is disabled:

git clone --branch add_cmake https://github.com/richefeu/mpmxdem.git ${MPMXDEM_SRC_DIR}
cmake -S ${MPMXDEM_SRC_DIR} -B build-mpmxdem -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      -DMPMXDEM_BUILD_2D=OFF \
      -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=${MPMXDEM_INSTALL_DIR}
cmake --build build-mpmxdem --target install -j10

Tip

Add -DFETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_TOOFUS=<path> to use a local copy of toofus instead of downloading it.

items.title: exaMPM installation
items.text:
git clone https://github.com/Collab4exaNBody/exaMPM.git ${EXAMPM_SRC_DIR}
source ${XNB_INSTALL_DIR}/bin/setup-env.sh   # also sources onika's environment
cmake -S ${EXAMPM_SRC_DIR} -B build-exampm -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      -Donika_DIR=${ONIKA_INSTALL_DIR} \
      -DexaNBody_DIR=${XNB_INSTALL_DIR} \
      -Dmpmxdem_DIR=${MPMXDEM_INSTALL_DIR} \
      -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=${EXAMPM_INSTALL_DIR}
cmake --build build-exampm -j10
ctest --test-dir build-exampm --output-on-failure
cmake --install build-exampm

ctest runs short versions of all the example decks (see Tests).

GPU support

exaMPM has no GPU option of its own: it is GPU-enabled when onika is built with ONIKA_BUILD_CUDA=ON. Sourcing exaNBody's setup-env.sh before configuring sets the right compilers.

items.title: Installed layout
items.text:
${EXAMPM_INSTALL_DIR}/
├── bin/
│   ├── exaMPM          # execution wrapper (sources setup-env.sh, then runs onika-exec)
│   └── setup-env.sh    # LD_LIBRARY_PATH, ONIKA_CONFIG_PATH, ONIKA_PLUGIN_PATH, ONIKA_DATA_PATH
├── lib/                # exaMPM plugins and exaNBody plugins rebuilt for the exaMPM grid
└── data/config/
    ├── main-config.msp     # default simulation graph, loaded by every run
    └── config_globals.msp  # default global values

items.title: Running your simulation
items.text:
exaMPM takes one input deck (a .msp YAML file). It first loads the default configuration data/config/main-config.msp, then the deck, which overrides it key by key.

${EXAMPM_INSTALL_DIR}/bin/exaMPM mydeck.msp      # installed
build-exampm/exaMPM mydeck.msp                   # from the build tree

Input files read by the deck (Blender geometry files, ...) are searched in the current directory, and outputs are written there (mpm_paraview/, ExaMPMOutputDir/).

items.title: Threads and GPU
items.text:
OpenMPGPU 
exaMPM mydeck.msp --omp_num_threads 8

The example decks set configuration: { nogpu: true }. Override it to run the kernels on the GPU:

exaMPM mydeck.msp --nogpu false --profiling-summary true

The profiling summary printed at the end shows the GPU time of each operator in parentheses.

MPI

mpirun -n N exaMPM starts, but MPM decks must run on one MPI process for now: material points are not migrated between processes.

items.title: Command-line options
items.text:
Any configuration key can be set from the command line: --a-b value sets configuration: { a: { b: value } }. Global values and slots of the graph are set with --set-<block>-<key> value:

# short run with more frequent outputs
exaMPM sphere_impacting_structure.msp --set-global-simulation_end_iteration 199 \
                                      --set-global-mpm_vtk_period 100

items.title: Getting help
items.text:
exaMPM --help plugins            # every available operator, by plugin
exaMPM --help set_mp_grid        # description and slots of one operator

WSL

On WSL2, init_cuda may print ERR: GPUs don't support unified memory, cannot continue and then go on: it is not a failure. Using all logical cores collapses performance when another process is running: use fewer threads.

items.title: Developer Guide
items.text:
exaMPM is an application on top of onika and exaNBody, organized like exaStamp and exaDEM: plugins of small operators, composed in YAML.

exaMPM/
├── CMakeLists.txt          # find_package(onika, exaNBody, mpmxdem), MPM field set, plugins
├── include/exaMPM/         # shared headers: fields, shape function, kernels, obstacles, setup helpers
├── src/                    # one plugin per directory, one operator per file
│   ├── grid/               #   exaMPMGrid: grid flavor, MPM nodes
│   ├── io/                 #   exaMPMIO: parameters, material point setup, log, outputs
│   ├── numericalscheme/    #   exaMPMNumericalScheme: P2G / grid update / G2P steps
│   ├── constitutivemodel/  #   exaMPMConstitutiveModel: mohr_coulomb, hooke_elasticity
│   ├── driver/             #   exaMPMDriver: obstacles and their motion, obstacle outputs
│   └── interaction/        #   exaMPMInteraction: contact laws and forces
├── data/config/            # main-config.msp, config_globals.msp
└── example/                # one folder per example: deck + files it reads (tests)
  • Adding an operator — file, slots, registration, YAML wiring
  • GPU kernels — writing a kernel once for OpenMP and CUDA
  • Coding rules — naming, logging, style
  • Tests — example decks as tests, CI

items.title: Files and namespaces
items.text:
• Headers are .h files under include/exaMPM/, with #pragma once.
  • Host-only operators are .cpp; operators that launch a kernel are .cu.
  • Code goes in namespace exaMPM { using namespace exanb; ... }. Fields are declared in include/exaMPM/fields.h with XNB_DECLARE_FIELD.

items.title: Naming
items.text:
• snake_case for operators, slots, YAML keys and functions; CamelCase for types; m_ prefix for members.
  • Operator names have no mpm_ prefix; YAML blocks of main-config.msp keep it (mpm_compute_loop, ...) to avoid clashes with exaNBody and onika names.
  • Grid-templated operators have a ...Tmpl alias; ONIKA_AUTORUN_INIT(<file basename>).

items.title: Operators
items.text:
• inline void execute() override final; every slot has a DocString; every operator implements documentation().
  • REQUIRED/OPTIONAL when there is no sane default; PRIVATE slots for persistent state.

items.title: Logging and errors
items.text: • lout (output), ldbg (debug, enabled with configuration: { debug: { filter: [ "regex" ] } }), lerr; fatal_error() << ... to abort. Never std::cout or printf.

items.title: Simplicity
items.text:
• exaMPM is a prototype: no speculative abstraction.
  • No new field set unless required: each one compiles every grid-templated operator once more.
  • Never modify onika or exaNBody from exaMPM: report the need upstream and work around it locally.

items.title: GPU Kernels
items.text: Kernels are written once, as functors, and run with OpenMP on the CPU or with CUDA on the GPU. The choice is made at run time (--nogpu false enables the GPU).

items.title: Per-material-point kernels
items.text: compute_mps(grid, mp_cells, func, pec, field::a, field::b, ...) (in include/exaMPM/mpm_gpu.h) calls func(a, b, ...) for every material point of the cells listed in mp_cells. Arguments are references for the fields the kernel writes. EXAMPM_GPU_PARTICLE_FUNCTOR(F) declares the functor GPU compatible.

items.title: Per-node kernels
items.text:
Node loops use onika's parallel_for over the cells; mpm_nodes(grid_cell_values) gives raw pointers to the nodal fields. EXAMPM_GPU_FOR_FUNCTOR(F) declares the functor GPU compatible:

struct GridMomentumRate
{
  MPMNodes nodes;
  double dt;
  ONIKA_HOST_DEVICE_FUNC void operator()(size_t c) const
  {
    const size_t i = c * nodes.stride;
    for (int d = 0; d < 3; d++)
    {
      nodes.qdot[i + d] = nodes.fb[i + d] + nodes.f[i + d];
      nodes.q[i + d] += nodes.qdot[i + d] * dt;
    }
  }
};
EXAMPM_GPU_FOR_FUNCTOR(GridMomentumRate)

// in execute():
onika::parallel::parallel_for(grid_cell_values->number_of_cells(),
                              GridMomentumRate{mpm_nodes(*grid_cell_values), *dt}, parallel_execution_context());

items.title: Rules inside a kernel
items.text:
• The functor is trivially copyable: values and raw pointers only, and a const call operator marked ONIKA_HOST_DEVICE_FUNC.
  • No virtual calls, STL containers, allocations, exceptions or logging.
  • Scatter to the nodes (P2G) with ONIKA_CU_ATOMIC_ADD.
  • Arrays read by a kernel (e.g. the obstacles, the contact laws) are copied to onika::memory::CudaMMVector (PRIVATE slots of the operator).
  • Small linear algebra: Vec3d, Mat3d and their functions (dot, cross, norm, transpose, ...) from onika, and include/exaMPM/mat9.h (port of toofus mat9, with the symmetric eigen decomposition used by Mohr-Coulomb).

Checking that a kernel runs on the GPU

Run with --nogpu false --profiling-summary true: the GPU time of each operator is printed in parentheses.

items.title: 1. Look for an existing one
items.text:
Before writing an operator, check that exaNBody or onika does not already provide it:

exaMPM --help plugins
grep -rn 'register_factory( *"<keyword>' ${XNB_SRC_DIR}/src ${ONIKA_SRC_DIR}/src

items.title: 2. Create the file
items.text: One operator per file, named after the operator, in the plugin directory that fits (src/<module>/<name>.cpp). Use .cu when the operator launches a kernel (compute_mps, parallel_for): it is compiled by nvcc when CUDA is enabled and as C++ otherwise. A plugin directory with only .cu files also needs a <module>_link_helper.cpp.

items.title: 3. Write it
items.text:
A complete example, update_mass (\(m_p = \rho_p V_p\)):

#include <exaMPM/mpm_gpu.h>
#include <exaMPM/mpm_operator.h>

namespace exaMPM
{
  struct UpdateMass   // the kernel: a POD functor, called for each material point
  {
    ONIKA_HOST_DEVICE_FUNC void operator()(double& mass, double density, double vol) const { mass = density * vol; }
  };
}  // namespace exaMPM
EXAMPM_GPU_PARTICLE_FUNCTOR(UpdateMass)   // may run on the GPU

namespace exaMPM
{
  template <class GridT, class = AssertGridHasFields<GridT, field::_mp_mass, field::_mp_density, field::_mp_vol>>
  struct UpdateMassNode : public OperatorNode
  {
    ADD_SLOT(GridT, grid, INPUT_OUTPUT, REQUIRED, DocString{"material points"});
    ADD_SLOT(CellList, mp_cells, INPUT, REQUIRED, DocString{"cells holding MPs"});

    inline std::string documentation() const override final { return "mpmxdem step 0: m_p = rho_p V_p."; }

    inline void execute() override final
    {
      compute_mps(*grid, *mp_cells, UpdateMass{}, parallel_execution_context(), field::mp_mass, field::mp_density,
                  field::mp_vol);
    }
  };

  template <class GridT> using UpdateMassTmpl = UpdateMassNode<GridT>;

  ONIKA_AUTORUN_INIT(update_mass)
  {
    OperatorNodeFactory::instance()->register_factory("update_mass", make_grid_variant_operator<UpdateMassTmpl>);
  }
}  // namespace exaMPM
  • Slots are declared with ADD_SLOT(type, name, flow, default, DocString{...}). flow is INPUT, OUTPUT, INPUT_OUTPUT or PRIVATE (persistent state of the operator); default is a value, REQUIRED or OPTIONAL.
  • Registration: make_grid_variant_operator<Tmpl> for an operator templated on the grid, make_simple_operator<T> otherwise.
  • The new file is picked up by the plugin's CMakeLists.txt (exampm_add_plugin), after re-running CMake.

items.title: 4. Wire it in YAML
items.text:
Put the operator in a hook of main-config.msp (application default) or of a deck. Never edit the simulation batch:

+mpm_log_extra:
  - my_operator: { my_slot: 1.0 }

items.title: 5. Test and document it
items.text: Check exaMPM --help my_operator, add an example folder example/<name>/ (deck <name>.msp and the files it reads) and a test to example/CMakeLists.txt (see Tests), and document the operator in this site.

items.title: Tests
items.text:
Every example deck is a test, registered in example/CMakeLists.txt:

add_omp_mpi_test(empty)        # 1 thread, 2 threads (_omp), mpirun -n 2 (_mpi)
add_omp_test(config_a1         # 1 thread, 2 threads (_omp); extra arguments are passed to exaMPM
             --set-global-simulation_end_iteration 99 --set-global-mpm_vtk_period 50)

MPM decks use add_omp_test (no MPI support yet) with a reduced number of steps, so that the whole suite runs in about a minute. Each example is a folder example/<name>/ holding <name>.msp and the files it reads. It is copied to <build>/example/<name>/ and its tests run there, so that their outputs stay out of the sources. <build>/example/exaMPM is a link to the exaMPM wrapper, so every example runs the same way:

cd build-exampm/example/piles_one && ../exaMPM piles_one.msp

ctest --test-dir build-exampm --output-on-failure
ctest --test-dir build-exampm -R Example_ExaMPM_config_a1

items.title: Continuous integration
items.text:
.github/workflows/install.yml (Ubuntu 24.04, mpich), on every push and pull request:

  1. builds onika and exaNBody from their main branches (cached by commit);
  2. builds and installs mpmxdem (branch add_cmake, without the 2D part);
  3. builds exaMPM, runs ctest and cmake --install;
  4. checks the installed files and runs the installed exaMPM on example/empty/empty.msp.

items.title: Comparing with mpmxdem
items.text:
The CMake target of mpmxdem gives the path of its mpmbox3D solver (MPMXDEM_MPMBOX3D). To compare a port:

  • use obstacles: { legacy_plane: true } and mpm_vtk_output: [ mpm_write_paraview, save_mp_pos ];
  • run both codes for the same number of steps on one thread;
  • compare mpm_mppos/mpPos<n>.txt with mpmxdem's mpPos<n>.txt (6 significant digits).

items.title: Main Features
items.text:
• YAML YAML-based input

    The whole simulation — setup, time loop, outputs — is a graph of operators described in YAML (.msp files). A user deck only overrides the blocks it needs from the default configuration.

    YAML basics

  • OpenMP x GPU

    All per-material-point and per-node kernels are written once and run with OpenMP or on NVIDIA GPUs (CUDA), selected at run time with --nogpu. MPI is not supported yet.

    Running

  • Background grid

    Regular grid of hexahedral elements with trilinear shape functions (RegularHexahedronLinear), one MPM node per exaNBody cell.

    Background Grid

  • Material points

    Cubic material points created in boxes, in Blender objects (prisms) or in closed STL meshes; moved, rotated, regrouped, and initialized with a geostatic K0 stress.

    Material Points

  • Constitutive models

    • Mohr-Coulomb elasto-plasticity with return mapping in the principal stress space
    • Linear (Hooke) elasticity
    • One model per material point group

    Constitutive Models

  • Rigid obstacles

    Spheres (fixed, driven or free), planes, cylinders and biplanar slopes, also read from Blender files; up to 9 obstacles. Penalty contact with friction per (material point group, obstacle group).

    Obstacles & Contacts

  • Outputs

    ParaView files of the material points and obstacle surfaces, a log line with global quantities and throughput, obstacle trajectories, and mpmxdem-compatible position files.

    Outputs

  • Validated against mpmxdem

    Each ported example is compared to mpmxdem: same material point count and positions within the output precision of mpmxdem.

    Tutorials

items.title: A little background
items.text: exaMPM is a Material Point Method (MPM) code. It stands for exascale Material Point Method.

items.title: What is exaMPM?
items.text:
The Material Point Method describes a continuum by a set of material points (MPs) that carry the mass, velocity, stress and history variables of the material, and a background grid on which the equations of motion are solved at each time step. Because the grid is reset at every step and the material points move freely through it, MPM handles very large deformations, free surfaces and contacts without mesh distortion: landslides, granular flows, impacts, penetration and soil-structure interaction.

exaMPM is built on the same software stack as exaStamp (molecular dynamics) and exaDEM (discrete elements):

  • onika provides the runtime: operators, the YAML simulation graph, OpenMP and CUDA parallelism, plugins.
  • exaNBody provides the particle grid (particles sorted in cells, stored as structures of arrays), per-cell values, domain decomposition and IO.
  • mpmxdem (richefeu/mpmxdem) is the reference MPM solver whose 3D part (mpmbox3D) exaMPM reproduces: shape functions, transfer scheme, constitutive models, obstacles and contact law, and the input commands of its .sim files.

items.title: Physics and numerical methods
items.text:
At each time step, exaMPM runs mpmxdem's modified Lagrangian (MUSL-like) algorithm:

  1. particle-to-grid transfer (P2G) of the mass, the internal forces \(-V_p\,\sigma_p\,\nabla N_I\), the gravity and the contact forces;
  2. integration of the nodal momentum;
  3. grid-to-particle transfer (G2P) of the velocity, then re-projection of the momentum on the grid;
  4. strain increment and stress update by the constitutive model of each material point;
  5. update of the volume and of the material point positions.

The background grid is a regular grid of hexahedra with trilinear shape functions. Rigid obstacles interact with the material points through a penalty contact law with friction. See Numerical Scheme for the details.

items.title: How MPM is mapped on exaNBody
items.text:
• Material points are exaNBody particles, with MPM fields (mp_mass, mp_vol, mp_stress, ...).
  • The MPM nodes are stored as exaNBody grid cell values, one node at the centre of each cell: the cell size is the MPM element size.
  • Each step of the algorithm is a small operator; the time loop is composed in YAML from these operators, so a user can reorder, replace or extend it without recompiling.
  • All per-MP and per-node kernels are written once as functors that run with OpenMP or on the GPU.

items.title: Status
items.text: exaMPM is a prototype. The five 3D examples of mpmxdem that can be ported are ported and validated against mpmxdem (see Tutorials). MPI runs are not supported yet: material points are not re-binned into cells when they move, and ghost exchanges of nodal values are not wired.

items.title: Versioning
items.text: exaMPM has no release yet: use the main branch. The version printed at startup comes from project(exaMPM VERSION ...) in CMakeLists.txt (currently 0.1.0).

items.title: Compatibility with onika, exaNBody & mpmxdem
items.text:
exaMPM exaNBody onika mpmxdem main main main branch add_cmake

The continuous integration of exaMPM builds onika and exaNBody from their main branches and mpmxdem from its add_cmake branch, so these are the combinations known to work.

items.title: Development notes
items.text:
Current development (main)

✨ Features

  • Port of the five portable 3D examples of mpmxdem: sphereImpactingStructure, config#A1, sphereOnSlope, slopeTwoLayers, piles_one.
  • Obstacles Sphere, Plane, Cylinder, LeftBiplanar and the Blender obstacles Plane2, Sphere2.
  • Material point setup: set_mp_grid, blender_set_mp_grid (coordinate files and STL), blender_modify_mp, move_mp, set_k0_stress.
  • Constitutive models mohr_coulomb and hooke_elasticity.
  • GPU port of every per-MP and per-node kernel.
  • exaDEM-like log line (simulation_state, print_simulation_state) and ParaView outputs of the obstacles.

🧪 Differences with mpmxdem

  • Plane and Plane2 tangent vectors are normalized (obstacles: { legacy_plane: true } restores mpmxdem's behaviour).
  • The constitutive model is chosen by material point group (see Constitutive Models).

items.text:

  year    = {2026},

items.title: mpmxdem
items.text: The physics of exaMPM (shape functions, modified Lagrangian scheme, Mohr-Coulomb model, obstacles and contact law) is ported from mpmxdem, an MPM code that can also embed periodic DEM simulations at the material points to build a numerically homogenized constitutive law.

items.title: Related codes
items.text:
• exaStamp — molecular dynamics on exaNBody (documentation)
  • exaDEM — discrete element method on exaNBody
  • onika, exaNBody — the underlying frameworks

items.title: Tutorials
items.text: The tutorials are the ports of the 3D examples of mpmxdem (mpm/3D/Examples/*.sim). Short versions of all of them run in ctest.

items.title: Running an example
items.text:
Each example is a folder of the exaMPM repository holding its deck, the files the deck reads and a picture:

example/
├── empty/                        empty.msp
├── sphere_impacting_structure/   sphere_impacting_structure.msp
├── config_a1/                    config_a1.msp
├── sphere_on_slope/              sphere_on_slope.msp  coordMP.txt  coordPlanes0..4.txt  coordSpheres.txt
├── slope_two_layers/             slope_two_layers.msp coordMP.txt  modifyMP.txt  coordPlanes0..4.txt
└── piles_one/                    piles_one.msp        slope.stl    coordPlanes0..4.txt

The build copies every folder to <build>/example/<name>/ (again whenever a file changes) and adds a link <build>/example/exaMPM to the exaMPM wrapper, so that every example runs the same way, in its own folder:

cd build-exampm/example/piles_one
../exaMPM piles_one.msp                                          # full run
../exaMPM piles_one.msp --set-global-simulation_end_iteration 19 # a few steps, as ctest

The decks read their input files from the run directory and write their outputs there (mpm_paraview/, ExaMPMOutputDir/), so the sources stay clean.

The pictures are made with ParaView, see Example images.

Not ported

slopeSoftLayer.sim is not ported: its only obstacle line is invalid (mpmxdem ignores it) and the format of its coordBoundaries.txt file is not documented.

Running the mpmxdem originals

The Blender examples use the nstep command, which mpmxdem 3D rejects at startup: they do not run as is in mpmxdem. exaMPM translates nstep 300000 into simulation_end_iteration: 299999.

items.title: Block sliding on a slope
items.text:
t = 0.009 s, the block on the inclined plane of the LeftBiplanar obstacle; colour: mean stress

A Mohr-Coulomb block (0.2 × 0.236 × 0.2 m, 8740 material points), tilted by 45° and under a K0 initial stress, slides down the inclined plane of a LeftBiplanar obstacle and spreads on its horizontal part. Port of mpmxdem's config#A1.sim.

items.title: Deck
items.text:
# mpmxdem mpm/3D/Examples/config#A1.sim: a Mohr-Coulomb block, tilted by 45 degrees and under K0 initial stress,
# slides down the inclined plane of a LeftBiplanar obstacle (plane + arc + inclined plane). SI units.

configuration:
  nogpu: true

global:
  dt: 1.0e-6
  simulation_end_iteration: 9999   # 0.01 s
  mpm_prox_period: 500

input_data:
  - parameters:
      gravity: [ 0.0 , -9.81 , 0.0 ]
  # MPM grid of 240 x 80 x 110 elements of 0.03 m
  - domain:
      cell_size: 0.03
      grid_dims: [ 241 , 81 , 111 ]
      bounds: [ [ -0.015 , -0.015 , -0.015 ] , [ 7.215 , 2.415 , 3.315 ] ]
      periodic: [ false , false , false ]
      expandable: false
  - grid_flavor_mpm
  - init_rcb_grid
  - set_mp_grid: { group: 0, density: 1890., lower: [ 2.87573593 , 0.5 , 1.25 ], upper: [ 3.07573593 , 0.736 , 1.45 ], size: 0.01 }
  - move_mp: { origin: [ 2.87573593 , 0.5 , 1.25 ], translation: [ -0.4 , 0.4 , 0.0 ], theta_z: 45.0 }
  - obstacles:
      obstacles: [ "LeftBiplanar 0 9 0.5 0 2.5 6 4 0.3 45" ]
  - contact_laws:
      set: [ "mu 0 0 0.3", "kn 0 0 1.0e6", "en2 0 0 0.2", "kt 0 0 0.5e6" ]
  - set_k0_stress: { nu: 0.42, density: 2000. }

init_epilog: mpm_init
compute_loop: mpm_compute_loop

mpm_constitutive_model:
  - mohr_coulomb: { group: 0, young: 80.0e4, poisson: 0.42, friction_angle: 0.5, cohesion: 1.0, dilatancy_angle: 0.05 }

items.title: Key points
items.text:
• set_mp_grid creates the block upright, then move_mp rotates it by 45° around its lower corner and moves it onto the slope.
  • set_k0_stress initializes the geostatic stress, with \(K_0 = \nu / (1 - \nu)\).
  • The grid is large (240 × 80 × 110 elements, 2.2 million nodes) for few material points: the per-node operators dominate the run time.

items.title: Run
items.text:
The folder example/config_a1/ holds the deck and its picture. In the build tree:

cd build-exampm/example/config_a1
../exaMPM config_a1.msp --omp_num_threads 8      # full run
../exaMPM config_a1.msp --set-global-simulation_end_iteration 99 --set-global-mpm_vtk_period 50   # short run (ctest)

Open mpm_paraview/mpm_*.pvtp (material points) and mpm_paraview/obstacles_*.vtk (obstacles) in ParaView.

items.title: Validation
items.text: After 2000 steps, exaMPM and mpmxdem have the same 8740 material points, and their positions differ by at most \(5.2 \times 10^{-6}\) m, the precision of mpmxdem's output files (6 digits).

items.text:
# mpmxdem mpm/3D/Examples/piles_one.sim: a fixed pile (Cylinder) through a Mohr-Coulomb slope in a box. SI units.
# Reads the Blender files of the original example from the run directory (not in mpmxdem). This folder holds
# small synthetic ones, used by the tests:
# slope.stl (slope) and coordPlanes0..4.txt (box).

configuration:
  nogpu: true

global:
  dt: 1.0e-5
  simulation_end_iteration: 299999   # mpmxdem: nstep 300000
  mpm_vtk_period: 2000

input_data:
  - parameters:
      gravity: [ 0.0 , -9.81 , 0.0 ]
  # mpmxdem new_set_grid 10 5 10 0.25: 40 x 20 x 40 elements of 0.25 m
  - domain:
      cell_size: 0.25
      grid_dims: [ 41 , 21 , 41 ]
      bounds: [ [ -0.125 , -0.125 , -0.125 ] , [ 10.125 , 5.125 , 10.125 ] ]
      periodic: [ false , false , false ]
      expandable: false
  - grid_flavor_mpm
  - init_rcb_grid
  - blender_set_mp_grid: { group: 0, density: 2000., file: slope.stl, format: stl, size: 0.125 }
  - obstacles:
      obstacles: [ "Plane2 0 coordPlanes0.txt", "Plane2 0 coordPlanes1.txt", "Plane2 0 coordPlanes2.txt",
                   "Plane2 0 coordPlanes3.txt", "Plane2 0 coordPlanes4.txt",
                   "Cylinder 1 5.5 0 3.0 0.4 4 0 1 0" ]
  - obstacles_delete_inside
  - contact_laws:
      set: [ "mu 0 0 0.0", "kn 0 0 1.0e6", "en2 0 0 1.0", "kt 0 0 0.5e6",
             "mu 0 1 0.3", "kn 0 1 1.0e6", "en2 0 1 1.0", "kt 0 1 0.5e6" ]

init_epilog: mpm_init
compute_loop: mpm_compute_loop

mpm_constitutive_model:
  - mohr_coulomb: { group: 0, young: 70.0e6, poisson: 0.42, friction_angle: 0.5, cohesion: 5.0e2, dilatancy_angle: 0.05 }

items.title: Key points
items.text:
• blender_set_mp_grid with format: stl fills a closed mesh with material points.
  • obstacles_delete_inside removes the material points inside the pile. As in mpmxdem, it ignores the length of the cylinder (see Cylinder).
  • The material/pile contact has no friction (mpmxdem's Cylinder has no tangents), whatever mu.

items.title: Input files
items.text: slope.stl and coordPlanes0..4.txt, read from the run directory. Synthetic files are provided in example/piles_one/ (a box-shaped slope).

items.title: Run
items.text:
The folder example/piles_one/ holds the deck, the synthetic slope.stl and coordPlanes0..4.txt, and its picture. In the build tree:

cd build-exampm/example/piles_one
../exaMPM piles_one.msp --omp_num_threads 8      # full run
../exaMPM piles_one.msp --set-global-simulation_end_iteration 19 --set-global-mpm_log_period 10   # short run (ctest)

To run the original example, replace the synthetic files of the run folder by the Blender files of the original.

Open mpm_paraview/mpm_*.pvtp (material points) and mpm_paraview/obstacles_*.vtk (obstacles) in ParaView.

items.text: With the files of example/piles_one/, exaMPM and mpmxdem create the same 40960 material points and both remove 880 of them inside the pile; positions after 2000 steps differ by less than \(6 \times 10^{-6}\) m.

A rigid sphere (R = 0.1 m, 30000 kg/m³) is thrown at 2 m/s against a cohesive Mohr-Coulomb block (0.4 × 0.5 × 2.4 m, 57000 material points) lying on a horizontal plane. Port of mpmxdem's sphereImpactingStructure.sim.

# SI units. Add '--nogpu false' to run on the GPU.

  nogpu: true

global:
  dt: 1.0e-5
  simulation_end_iteration: 49999   # 0.5 s

input_data:

      gravity: [ 0.0 , -9.81 , 0.0 ]
  # MPM grid of 100 x 40 x 55 elements of 0.06 m: one exaNBody cell per node, domain shifted by -h/2

      bounds: [ [ -0.03 , -0.03 , -0.03 ] , [ 6.03 , 2.43 , 3.33 ] ]
      periodic: [ false , false , false ]
      expandable: false

  - init_rcb_grid
  - set_mp_grid: { group: 0, density: 2000., lower: [ 3.5 , 0.5 , 0.3 ], upper: [ 3.9 , 1.0 , 2.7 ], size: 0.02 }
  - obstacles:
      obstacles:
        - "Sphere 0 3.1 1.0 1.4 0.1 free 30000.0 2.0 0.1 0 0"
        - "Plane 1 0.0 0.5 0.0 8.0 0.5 0.0 8.0 0.5 4.0 0.0 0.5 4.0"
  - contact_laws:
      set: [ "mu 0 0 0.3", "kn 0 0 1.0e6", "en2 0 0 0.8", "kt 0 0 0.5e6",
             "mu 0 1 1.0", "kn 0 1 1.0e6", "en2 0 1 0.8", "kt 0 1 0.5e6" ]

init_epilog: mpm_init
compute_loop: mpm_compute_loop

mpm_constitutive_model:
  - mohr_coulomb: { group: 0, young: 8.0e6, poisson: 0.42, friction_angle: 0.7, cohesion: 1e4, dilatancy_angle: 0.05 }

items.title: Key points
items.text:
• Grid: 100 × 40 × 55 elements of 0.06 m, i.e. grid_dims: [101, 41, 56] and a domain starting at −0.03.
  • Material points: 3 per element and direction (size: 0.02).
  • Obstacles: the sphere is group 0 and the plane group 1; the block has two contact laws, with \(\mu = 0.3\) on the sphere and \(\mu = 1\) on the floor.
  • Duration: 50000 steps of \(10^{-5}\) s, i.e. 0.5 s.

items.title: Run
items.text:
The folder example/sphere_impacting_structure/ holds the deck and its picture. In the build tree:

cd build-exampm/example/sphere_impacting_structure
../exaMPM sphere_impacting_structure.msp --omp_num_threads 8      # full run
../exaMPM sphere_impacting_structure.msp --set-global-simulation_end_iteration 199 --set-global-mpm_vtk_period 100   # short run (ctest)

Add --nogpu false to run the kernels on the GPU.

Open mpm_paraview/mpm_*.pvtp (material points) and mpm_paraview/obstacles_*.vtk (obstacles) in ParaView.

Add mpm_log_extra: print_obstacles to the deck (or --set-mpm_log_extra print_obstacles) to follow the sphere. The sphere hits the block after about 0.15 s.

Comparing with mpmxdem

mpmxdem's plane vectors are not normalized (see Plane). Use obstacles: { legacy_plane: true } to compare with mpmxdem's results, and compare before the impact or with a tolerance: the atomic sums make multi-threaded runs not bitwise reproducible.
