items.title: User guide to exaMPM
items.text:
This is the reference section of the documentation: the default simulation graph, the background grid, the material points and how to create them, the constitutive models, the obstacles and their contact law, the time scheme and the outputs.

For a guided introduction, see the Beginner Guide tab.

  • Simulation Graph — the default configuration, its hooks and MPM blocks
  • Background Grid — MPM nodes on the exaNBody cells, shape functions
  • Material Points — fields, setup operators and Blender geometry files
  • Constitutive Models — Mohr-Coulomb and Hooke elasticity
  • Obstacles & Contacts — rigid obstacles and the material point-obstacle contact law
  • Numerical Scheme — the modified Lagrangian time step, operator by operator
  • Outputs — log, ParaView files, visualization
  • Exhaustive Operator List — every exaMPM operator and its slots

Note

The list of operators available in your build, with their slots, is printed by exaMPM --help plugins and exaMPM --help <operator_name>.

items.title: Constitutive Models
items.text:
The constitutive models update the strain and the stress of the material points at step 4 of the time scheme. They are listed in the hook mpm_constitutive_model, one operator per group of material points:

mpm_constitutive_model:
  - hooke_elasticity: { group: 0, young: 200.0e8, poisson: 0.42 }
  - mohr_coulomb: { group: 1, young: 70.0e6, poisson: 0.42, friction_angle: 0.5, cohesion: 50., dilatancy_angle: 0.05 }

group: -1 (the default) applies the model to all the material points. A group with no model keeps its stress.

items.title: Strain increment
items.text:
All models start from the same strain increment, computed from the nodal velocities \(\mathbf{v}_I = \mathbf{q}_I / m_I\) of the nodes heavier than tolmass:

\[ \Delta\varepsilon_p = \frac{\Delta t}{2} \sum_I \left(\mathbf{v}_I \otimes \nabla N_I(\mathbf{x}_p) + \nabla N_I(\mathbf{x}_p) \otimes \mathbf{v}_I\right), \qquad \varepsilon_p \leftarrow \varepsilon_p + \Delta\varepsilon_p . \] Model Operator mpmxdem Mohr-Coulomb mohr_coulomb MohrCoulomb Linear elasticity hooke_elasticity HookeElasticity

Both models run on the GPU.

items.title: Description
items.text:
Isotropic linear elasticity, ported from mpmxdem's HookeElasticity. The stress is computed from the total strain:

\[ \sigma_{ii} = rac{E}{(1+ u)(1-2 u)}\left[(1- u)\,\varepsilon_{ii} + u \sum_{j e i} \varepsilon_{jj} ight], \qquad \sigma_{ij} = G\,\varepsilon_{ij} \;\; (i e j), \quad G = rac{E}{2(1+ u)} . \]

Shear terms

As in mpmxdem, the shear stress is \(G\,\varepsilon_{ij}\) with the tensor strain \(\varepsilon_{ij}\) (half the engineering shear strain), i.e. half the shear stress of the usual Hooke law. The Mohr-Coulomb elastic predictor uses the same convention.

Because the stress is recomputed from the total strain, an initial stress (e.g. set_k0_stress) is overwritten at the first step, as in mpmxdem.

items.title: YAML syntax
items.text:
hooke_elasticity:
  group: VALUE     # MP group, -1 for all
  young: VALUE     # Young modulus E (Pa)
  poisson: VALUE   # Poisson ratio nu

young and poisson are required.

items.title: Usage example
items.text:
Stiff elastic slope with a weak Mohr-Coulomb layer (slope_two_layers)

mpm_constitutive_model:
  - hooke_elasticity: { group: 0, young: 200.0e8, poisson: 0.42 }
  - mohr_coulomb: { group: 1, young: 70.0e6, poisson: 0.42, friction_angle: 0.5, cohesion: 5.0e1, dilatancy_angle: 0.05 }

items.title: Description
items.text:
Elastic-perfectly plastic Mohr-Coulomb model with a non-associated flow rule, ported from mpmxdem's MohrCoulomb.

  1. Elastic predictor, with the isotropic stiffness \(D^e\) (\(E\), \(\nu\)): \(\sigma \leftarrow \sigma + D^e : \Delta\varepsilon\) (shear terms \(G\,\Delta\varepsilon_{ij}\), as in mpmxdem, see Hooke).

  2. Return mapping in the principal stress space \(\sigma_1 \ge \sigma_2 \ge \sigma_3\). For each pair of principal stresses \((a, b) \in \{(2,3), (1,3), (1,2)\}\), the yield function

    \[ f_{ab} = \tfrac{1}{2}\left|\sigma_a - \sigma_b\right| + \tfrac{1}{2}(\sigma_a + \sigma_b)\sin\varphi - c\cos\varphi \]

    is brought back to 0 when positive, with the plastic potential \(g\) of the same form using the dilatancy angle \(\psi\) instead of \(\varphi\). The correction is accumulated in mp_plastic_stress. 3. The stress is rotated back from the principal axes.

The three return-mapping cases are those of mpmxdem (yield functions of Ceccato's thesis), reproduced bitwise.

items.title: YAML syntax
items.text:
mohr_coulomb:
  group: VALUE            # MP group, -1 for all
  young: VALUE            # Young modulus E (Pa)
  poisson: VALUE          # Poisson ratio nu
  friction_angle: VALUE   # phi (rad)
  cohesion: VALUE         # c (Pa)
  dilatancy_angle: VALUE  # psi (rad)
Parameter Units Default group — -1 young Pa 200e6 poisson — 0.2 friction_angle rad 0.5 cohesion Pa 0 dilatancy_angle rad 0.3

items.title: Usage example
items.text:
Cohesive soil block (sphere_impacting_structure)

mpm_constitutive_model:
  - mohr_coulomb: { group: 0, young: 8.0e6, poisson: 0.42, friction_angle: 0.7, cohesion: 1e4, dilatancy_angle: 0.05 }

Angles in radians

mpmxdem's .sim files give the angles in radians: friction_angle: 0.5 is 28.6°.

items.title: Nodes on exaNBody cells
items.text:
The MPM background grid is a regular grid of cubic elements of size \(h\). exaMPM stores it in exaNBody's grid cell values with one node per cell: node \((i, j, k)\) is the centre of cell \((i, j, k)\), at \(\mathbf{x}_I = (i h, j h, k h)\) when the domain starts at \(-h/2\) (see Domain).

init_nodes (in mpm_init) adds the nodal fields:

Field Components Meaning (mpmxdem name) mpm_mass 1 nodal mass \(m_I\) (mass) mpm_q 3 nodal momentum \(\mathbf{q}_I\) (q) mpm_qdot 3 nodal momentum rate \(\dot{\mathbf{q}}_I\) (qdot) mpm_f 3 internal and gravity forces \(\mathbf{f}_I\) (f) mpm_fb 3 contact (boundary) forces \(\mathbf{f}^b_I\) (fb)

All the nodal values are reset at each step (reset_nodes).

items.title: Shape functions
items.text:
exaMPM uses mpmxdem's RegularHexahedronLinear: the 8 nodes of the element that contains the material point, with trilinear shape functions

\[ N_I(\mathbf{x}_p) = \prod_{d \in \{x,y,z\}} \left(1 - \frac{|x_{p,d} - x_{I,d}|}{h}\right), \qquad \frac{\partial N_I}{\partial x} = -\frac{\operatorname{sign}(x_p - x_I)}{h} \left(1 - \frac{|y_p - y_I|}{h}\right)\left(1 - \frac{|z_p - z_I|}{h}\right). \]

Nodes lighter than tolmass (slot of parameters, default 1e-6) are ignored in the grid-to-particle transfers.

items.title: Cells holding material points
items.text:
Most cells of an MPM grid hold no material point. update_mp_cells lists the cells that hold some (slot mp_cells) at the beginning of each step, and every per-material-point kernel loops over these cells only.

Material points are not re-binned

Material points stay in the cell where they were created; their nodes are always found from their position. This is why MPI is not supported yet.

Performance

The per-node operators (reset_nodes, grid_momentum_rate) loop over all the nodes. On large, mostly empty grids (e.g. config#A1: 2.2 million nodes for 8740 material points) they dominate the run time.

items.title: Material Points
items.text:
Material points (MPs) are exaNBody particles of the exaMPM grid type (grid_flavor_mpm). Each one represents a cube of material of side size and carries its mass, velocity, stress and history variables.

  • Fields — the per-material-point fields and their mpmxdem names
  • Setters — operators that create, move, regroup and initialize material points
  • Blender files — formats of the Blender coordinate and STL files

items.title: Groups
items.text:
The group of a material point (built-in field type, mpmxdem groupNb) selects:

  • its constitutive model (slot group of mohr_coulomb, hooke_elasticity);
  • its contact laws with each obstacle group (contact_laws).

Groups are integers from 0 to 255.

items.title: Blender Geometry Files
items.text:
Some mpmxdem examples describe their geometry with files exported from Blender. exaMPM reads the same files. All the files are text files, read from the run directory (blender_folder for the obstacles).

Axes

Blender's vertical axis is z, exaMPM's is y. All the readers swap y and z: a Blender vertex x y z is the exaMPM point (x, z, y).

items.title: Coordinate files (coordMP.txt, modifyMP.txt)
items.text:
Used by blender_set_mp_grid (format: coords) and blender_modify_mp. One block per object: the word Object, the number of vertices, then the vertices (Blender axes).

Object 8
1 1 0.5
9 1 0.5
9 1 3.5
5 1 3.5
1 5 0.5
9 5 0.5
9 5 3.5
5 5 3.5

Each object must be a prism along exaMPM's z axis (Blender's y): exaMPM takes the distinct (x, y) vertices, sorts them by angle around their mean to get the cross-section polygon, and fills the bounding box of the object with the material points inside this polygon.

items.title: STL files
items.text:
Used by blender_set_mp_grid with format: stl: an ASCII STL file of a closed mesh (Blender: File > Export > STL, ASCII checked). A point is inside the mesh when a ray along +x crosses an odd number of triangles.

solid slope
 facet normal 0 0 0
  outer loop
   vertex 1 1 0.5
   vertex 1 1 3
   vertex 1 5 3
  endloop
 endfacet
 ...
endsolid slope

items.title: Plane files (coordPlanes<i>.txt)
items.text:
Used by the Plane2 obstacle: a name, the number of vertices (4) and the 4 vertices of a rectangle (Blender axes). The coordinates are rounded to 0.01, as in mpmxdem.

floor 4
0.75 0.75 0.5
9.5 0.75 0.5
0.75 5.25 0.5
9.5 5.25 0.5

The vertices are, in order: the origin, the end of the first edge, the end of the second edge and the opposite corner. The normal of the plane is \(-\mathbf{t}_1 \times \mathbf{t}_2\) with \(\mathbf{t}_1\), \(\mathbf{t}_2\) the two edges.

items.title: Sphere files (coordSpheres.txt)
items.text:
Used by the Sphere2 obstacle: a name, the radius and the centre (Blender axes).

ball 0.4 6.5 3 4

Generating the files

In mpmxdem, these files are produced by a Blender Python script (getCoord) that is not distributed with mpmxdem. The example folders of exaMPM (example/<name>/) contain small hand-written files used by the tests.

items.title: Material Point Fields
items.text:
All the material points share one field set, MPMFieldSet (declared in include/exaMPM/fields.h):

Field Type Meaning mpmxdem (MaterialPoint) rx, ry, rz double position pos vx, vy, vz double velocity vel fx, fy, fz double contact force from the obstacles f id uint64 identifier index in MP type uint8 group groupNb mp_mass double mass mass mp_vol double volume vol mp_density double mass density density mp_stress Mat3d total stress \(\sigma\) stress mp_strain Mat3d total strain \(\varepsilon\) strain mp_plastic_stress Mat3d cumulated plastic stress correction plasticStress mp_delta_strain Mat3d strain increment of the step, used for the volume update deltaStrain mp_prev_pos Vec3d position at the previous step (friction) prev_pos mp_contact_dn, _fn, _ft1, _ft2 Mat3d contact history with each obstacle Neighbor::dn, fn, ft

The contact history fields hold one value per obstacle: component o (m11, m12, ..., m33) is the history for obstacle o, hence at most 9 obstacles.

The ParaView output writes id, type, vx, vy, vz, mp_mass, mp_vol, mp_stress and mp_strain by default (see Outputs).

items.title: Material Point Setters
items.text: These operators run once, in input_data, after grid_flavor_mpm and init_rcb_grid. They can be chained: each set_* operator adds material points to those already created, and the other operators act on all the existing material points.

items.title: set_mp_grid
items.text:
Fills a box with cubic material points of side size, at rest and stress free (mpmxdem: set_MP_grid).

- set_mp_grid: { group: 0, density: 2000., lower: [ 3.5 , 0.5 , 0.3 ], upper: [ 3.9 , 1.0 , 2.7 ], size: 0.02 }
Slot Description Default group material point group 0 density mass density required lower, upper corners of the box required size side of the material points required

items.title: blender_set_mp_grid
items.text:
Fills a Blender object with material points of side size. The material point centres are on a lattice that starts at the lower corner of the bounding box of the object + size/2 (mpmxdem: blender_set_MP_grid and blender_set_MP_grid2).

- blender_set_mp_grid: { group: 0, density: 2000., file: coordMP.txt, size: 0.125 }            # prisms
- blender_set_mp_grid: { group: 0, density: 2000., file: slope.stl, format: stl, size: 0.125 }  # closed mesh
Slot Description Default group material point group 0 density mass density required file geometry file (read from the run directory) required format coords: Object n x y z ... file, each object being a prism along z; stl: ASCII STL closed mesh coords size side of the material points required

The run aborts if the cell size is more than 3 times size (same check as mpmxdem). File formats: Blender files.

items.title: blender_modify_mp
items.text:
Gives a new group and density to the material points inside the objects of a Blender coordinate file (mpmxdem: blender_modify_MP). The mass is updated. As in mpmxdem, the material points of the lowest and highest z layers are left unchanged.

- blender_modify_mp: { group: 1, density: 2000., file: modifyMP.txt }
Slot Description group new group (selects the constitutive model and contact laws) density new mass density file Object n x y z ... Blender coordinate file

Difference with mpmxdem

mpmxdem's blender_modify_MP changes the constitutive model of the material points but keeps their group. In exaMPM the model is chosen by group, so the modified material points get a new group, and the deck must define the contact laws of this group too (see slope_two_layers).

items.title: move_mp
items.text:
Rotates all the material points around origin (rotation \(R = R_z(\theta_z)\,R_y(\theta_y)\)), then translates them (mpmxdem: move_MP). The previous position is moved too.

- move_mp: { origin: [ 2.87573593 , 0.5 , 1.25 ], translation: [ -0.4 , 0.4 , 0.0 ], theta_z: 45.0 }
Slot Description Default origin centre of the rotations [0, 0, 0] translation translation applied after the rotation [0, 0, 0] theta_z rotation around z (degrees, negative is clockwise) 0 theta_y rotation around y (degrees) 0

items.title: set_k0_stress
items.text:
Geostatic initial stress (mpmxdem: set_K0_stress). With \(d\) the depth along the gravity below the highest material point:

\[ \sigma_{yy} = -d\,g\,\rho_0, \qquad \sigma_{xx} = K_0\,\sigma_{yy}, \qquad \sigma_{xy} = \sigma_{yx} = 0, \qquad K_0 = \frac{\nu}{1-\nu}. \]

The other components are left unchanged, as in mpmxdem.

- set_k0_stress: { nu: 0.42, density: 2000. }
Slot Description gravity gravity (taken from parameters by default) nu Poisson ratio used for \(K_0\) density density of the overburden \(\rho_0\)

items.title: Numerical Scheme
items.text:
One time step is the batch mpm_modified_lagrangian, mpmxdem's ModifiedLagrangian::advanceOneStep split into operators. Notations: \(p\) material points, \(I\) nodes, \(N_I = N_I(\mathbf{x}_p)\).

# Operator Computation update_mp_cells list of the cells holding material points A obstacles_reset obstacle force and moment set to 0, acceleration set to gravity zero_particle_force material point contact forces set to 0 reset_nodes all nodal values set to 0 B obstacles_predict obstacle motion: position and first half velocity update (free), \(\mathbf{x} \mathrel{+}= \mathbf{v}\Delta t\) (imposed velocity) 0 update_mass \(m_p = \rho_p V_p\) 1 p2g_mass \(m_I = \sum_p N_I\, m_p\) (aborts if a material point is outside the grid) 2 p2g_internal_forces \(\mathbf{f}_I = \sum_p \left(-V_p\,\sigma_p \nabla N_I + m_p\,\mathbf{g}\,N_I\right)\) 2b contact_forces material point-obstacle contact forces (contact law) C obstacles_correct second half velocity update of the free obstacles p2g_contact_forces \(\mathbf{f}^b_I = \sum_p N_I\,\mathbf{f}_p\) 3 grid_momentum_rate \(\dot{\mathbf{q}}_I = \mathbf{f}^b_I + \mathbf{f}_I\), \(\mathbf{q}_I \mathrel{+}= \dot{\mathbf{q}}_I\,\Delta t\) 3a g2p_velocity \(\mathbf{v}_p \mathrel{+}= \Delta t \sum_I N_I\, \dot{\mathbf{q}}_I / m_I\) 3b p2g_momentum \(\mathbf{q}_I = \sum_p N_I\, m_p \mathbf{v}_p\) (nodal momentum recomputed from the updated velocities) 4 mpm_constitutive_model strain increment and stress (constitutive models) 4a update_volume volume and density from mp_delta_strain 5 g2p_position \(\mathbf{x}_p^{prev} = \mathbf{x}_p\), \(\mathbf{x}_p \mathrel{+}= \Delta t \sum_I N_I\, \mathbf{q}_I / m_I\)

Sums over \(I\) only use the nodes heavier than tolmass.

Reproduced mpmxdem quirks

The scheme is reproduced as is, including:

  • the volume update uses only \(\Delta\varepsilon_{xx} + \Delta\varepsilon_{yy}\) (2D formula) of mp_delta_strain, which neither mohr_coulomb nor hooke_elasticity fills (as in mpmxdem): the volume and the density of the material points stay constant;
  • the gravity only enters the first half velocity update of the free obstacles.

Reproducibility

p2g_* and contact_forces sum with atomic additions: two identical multi-threaded or GPU runs differ by round-off (about \(10^{-3}\) relative on the obstacle force after the impact of the sphere example).

items.title: Obstacles & Contacts
items.text:
Rigid obstacles interact with the material points through a penalty contact law. They are created by the obstacles operator, one definition line per obstacle, with the syntax of mpmxdem's Obstacle and blender_Obstacle commands:

- obstacles:
    obstacles:
      - "Sphere 0 3.1 1.0 1.4 0.1 free 30000.0 2.0 0.1 0 0"
      - "Plane 1 0.0 0.5 0.0 8.0 0.5 0.0 8.0 0.5 4.0 0.0 0.5 4.0"
    blender_folder: "."      # folder of the Plane2 / Sphere2 files
    legacy_plane: false      # true: reproduce mpmxdem's plane bug

The second word of each line is the obstacle group, used by the contact laws.

Type Line Motion Page Sphere Sphere group xc yc zc R driveMode ... fixed, imposed velocity or free Sphere Plane Plane group x0 y0 z0 x1 y1 z1 x2 y2 z2 x3 y3 z3 fixed Plane Cylinder Cylinder group x y z R length dx dy dz fixed Cylinder LeftBiplanar LeftBiplanar group x0 y0 z0 lengthz l1 l2 R angle fixed LeftBiplanar Plane2 Plane2 group file fixed Blender obstacles Sphere2 Sphere2 group file driveMode ... as Sphere Blender obstacles

At most 9 obstacles can be defined. As in mpmxdem, the Blender obstacles (Plane2, Sphere2) are put after the others: obstacle indices (in the logs and outputs) follow this order. The obstacles are listed at startup:

obstacle 0: Sphere group=0 free mass=1.2566370614e+02
obstacle 1: Plane group=1 driven mass=0.0000000000e+00

items.title: Operators
items.text: Operator Role obstacles creates the obstacles (setup) obstacles_delete_inside removes the material points overlapping a Cylinder (setup) contact_laws contact parameters per (MP group, obstacle group) (setup) obstacles_reset, obstacles_predict, obstacles_correct obstacle motion, in each step contact_forces material point-obstacle contact forces, in each step check_proximity periodic reset of the contact history (mpm_prox_period) print_obstacles log of the free obstacles paraview_obstacles VTK surfaces of the obstacles

items.title: Blender Obstacles
items.text: Plane2 and Sphere2 are a Plane and a Sphere whose geometry is read from a file exported from Blender (mpmxdem: blender_Obstacle). The files are read from blender_folder (default: the run directory); their formats are given in Blender files.

items.title: YAML syntax
items.text:
- obstacles:
    obstacles:
      - "Plane2 group file"                 # e.g. coordPlanes0.txt
      - "Sphere2 group file driveMode ..."  # e.g. coordSpheres.txt, same driveMode as Sphere
    blender_folder: "."
  • Plane2 vertices are rounded to 0.01, as in mpmxdem, and its vectors are normalized unless legacy_plane: true.
  • Blender obstacles are placed after the other obstacles, whatever their order in the list.

items.title: Usage example
items.text:
A box of 5 planes and a free sphere (sphere_on_slope)

obstacles: [ "Plane2 0 coordPlanes0.txt", "Plane2 0 coordPlanes1.txt", "Plane2 0 coordPlanes2.txt",
             "Plane2 0 coordPlanes3.txt", "Plane2 0 coordPlanes4.txt",
             "Sphere2 1 coordSpheres.txt free 2700.0 0.0 0.0 0.0 0.0" ]

items.title: Description
items.text:
The force between a material point and an obstacle (mpmxdem: MPMbox::boundaryConditions) is computed by contact_forces at each step, for every (material point, obstacle) pair in contact (\(d_n < 0\)), with the parameters of the pair (MP group, obstacle group):

Normal force (incremental, with the previous distance \(d_n^{old}\)):

\[ f_n \leftarrow \begin{cases} -k_n\,e_n^2\,d_n & \text{unloading } (d_n > d_n^{old})\\ f_n - k_n\,(d_n - d_n^{old}) & \text{loading } (d_n < d_n^{old})\\ -k_n\,d_n & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \]

Friction along each tangent \(\mathbf{t}_k\), from the relative displacement over the step, with Coulomb's limit:

\[ f_{t,k} \leftarrow \operatorname{clamp}\left(f_{t,k} - k_t\left[(\mathbf{x}_p - \mathbf{x}_p^{prev}) - \Delta t\,\mathbf{v}_{obst}\right]\cdot\mathbf{t}_k,\; -\mu f_n,\; \mu f_n\right) \]

The force \(\mathbf{f} = f_n\mathbf{n} + f_{t,1}\mathbf{t}_1 + f_{t,2}\mathbf{t}_2\) is added to the material point (fx, fy, fz, then to the nodes by p2g_contact_forces) and \(-\mathbf{f}\) to the obstacle. The history (\(d_n\), \(f_n\), \(f_{t,1}\), \(f_{t,2}\)) is stored per material point and obstacle, and reset when the contact is lost.

check_proximity, every mpm_prox_period steps, mimics mpmxdem's neighbor list rebuild: it resets \(d_n\) and, except for planes, \(f_{t,2}\).

items.title: YAML syntax
items.text:
- contact_laws:
    set: [ "<mu|kn|en2|kt> groupMP groupObst value", ... ]
Parameter Description kn normal stiffness kt tangential stiffness en2 unloading factor (square of the restitution coefficient) mu friction coefficient

A (MP group, obstacle group) pair without a law has all parameters equal to 0: no contact force.

items.title: Usage example
items.text:
Two obstacle groups

- contact_laws:
    set: [ "mu 0 0 0.3", "kn 0 0 1.0e6", "en2 0 0 0.8", "kt 0 0 0.5e6",
           "mu 0 1 1.0", "kn 0 1 1.0e6", "en2 0 1 0.8", "kt 0 1 0.5e6" ]

items.title: Description
items.text:
A fixed rigid cylinder of radius \(R\) and length \(L\), starting at \(\mathbf{x}_0\) along the unit axis \(\mathbf{a}\) (mpmxdem: Cylinder). A material point touches it when \(0 \le (\mathbf{x}_p - \mathbf{x}_0)\cdot\mathbf{a} \le L\) and its distance to the axis minus \(R\) and \(\frac{1}{2}V_p^{1/3}\) is negative.

mpmxdem behaviour

  • The contact has no friction: mpmxdem leaves the tangents to zero.
  • obstacles_delete_inside removes the material points closer than \(R + \frac{1}{2}V_p^{1/3}\) to the axis line, ignoring the length of the cylinder, like mpmxdem's deleteIfInside.

items.title: YAML syntax
items.text:
input_data:
  - [...]                               # material points first
  - obstacles:
      obstacles: [ "Cylinder group x y z R length dx dy dz" ]
  - obstacles_delete_inside             # optional: remove the MPs inside the cylinder

The axis \((d_x, d_y, d_z)\) is normalized.

items.title: Usage example
items.text:
Vertical pile of radius 0.4 m and length 4 m (piles_one)

obstacles: [ "Cylinder 1 5.5 0 3.0 0.4 4 0 1 0" ]

items.title: Description
items.text:
A fixed slope made of a horizontal plane, a circular arc and an inclined plane, extruded along z (mpmxdem: LeftBiplanar):

  • the horizontal plane goes from \(\mathbf{x}_0\) towards \(-x\) over a length \(l_1\);
  • an arc of radius \(R\) and angle \(\alpha\) (degrees) connects it to
  • an inclined plane of length \(l_2\), at the angle \(\alpha\) from the horizontal, going up towards \(-x\);
  • all three extend from \(z_0\) to $z_0 + $ lengthz.

A material point touches the arc first, else the horizontal plane, else the inclined plane. The arc contact normal points towards the arc centre, with \(\mathbf{t}_2 = \mathbf{e}_z\).

items.title: YAML syntax
items.text:
- obstacles:
    obstacles: [ "LeftBiplanar group x0 y0 z0 lengthz l1 l2 R angle" ]

items.title: Usage example
items.text:
45° slope ending on a 6 m flat floor (config_a1)

obstacles: [ "LeftBiplanar 0 9 0.5 0 2.5 6 4 0.3 45" ]

items.title: Description
items.text:
A rigid rectangle given by its 4 corners \(\mathbf{p}_0 \dots \mathbf{p}_3\) (clockwise). Its tangents are \(\mathbf{t}_1 = \mathbf{p}_1 - \mathbf{p}_0\) and \(\mathbf{t}_2 = \mathbf{p}_3 - \mathbf{p}_0\), its normal \(\mathbf{n} = -\mathbf{t}_1 \times \mathbf{t}_2\) (all three normalized). A material point touches the plane when its projection lies inside the rectangle and

\[ d_n = (\mathbf{x}_p - \mathbf{p}_0)\cdot\mathbf{n} - \tfrac{1}{2}V_p^{1/3} < 0 . \]

The plane acts on one side only: choose the order of the corners so that \(\mathbf{n}\) points towards the material.

items.title: YAML syntax
items.text:
- obstacles:
    obstacles: [ "Plane group x0 y0 z0 x1 y1 z1 x2 y2 z2 x3 y3 z3" ]
    legacy_plane: false

legacy_plane

mpmxdem calls vec3r::normalized(), which returns a normalized copy and leaves the vectors unchanged: its plane vectors are not normalized, so the plane only acts on a smaller rectangle. exaMPM normalizes them; legacy_plane: true reproduces mpmxdem (for comparisons only). It also applies to Plane2.

The tangential contact history of a plane is kept by check_proximity (mpmxdem behaviour).

items.title: Usage example
items.text:
Horizontal floor at y = 0.5 m, normal +y

obstacles: [ "Plane 1 0.0 0.5 0.0 8.0 0.5 0.0 8.0 0.5 4.0 0.0 0.5 4.0" ]

items.title: Description
items.text:
A rigid sphere of centre \(\mathbf{x}_c\) and radius \(R\). A material point of volume \(V_p\) touches it when

\[ d_n = \|\mathbf{x}_p - \mathbf{x}_c\| - R - \tfrac{1}{2}V_p^{1/3} < 0 . \]

The contact normal is \(\mathbf{n} = (\mathbf{x}_p - \mathbf{x}_c)/\|\mathbf{x}_p - \mathbf{x}_c\|\), with the tangents \(\mathbf{t}_1 = (-n_y, n_x, 0)\) and \(\mathbf{t}_2 = (0, n_z, -n_y)\) (as in mpmxdem; they are not normalized).

items.title: YAML syntax
items.text:
- obstacles:
    obstacles: [ "Sphere group xc yc zc R driveMode ..." ]
driveMode Following values Motion freeze — fixed velocity density vx vy vz imposed velocity (the density is read but unused) free density vx vy vz vrot free rigid body: mass \(\frac{4}{3}\pi R^3\rho\), inertia \(\frac{2}{5} m R^2\), initial velocities

A free sphere moves under gravity and the contact forces of the material points (velocity Verlet: obstacles_predict, then obstacles_correct after contact_forces). As in mpmxdem, the gravity only contributes to the first half velocity update.

items.title: Usage example
items.text:
Free sphere thrown at 2 m/s (sphere_impacting_structure)

obstacles: [ "Sphere 0 3.1 1.0 1.4 0.1 free 30000.0 2.0 0.1 0 0" ]

items.title: Exhaustive Operator List
items.text: Every operator of exaMPM, by plugin, with its slots (exaMPM --help <operator> prints the same information for your build). Slots read from the global data graph (dt, gravity, mp_cells, grid, ...) are usually not set in YAML. exaNBody and onika operators used by exaMPM (domain, init_rcb_grid, write_paraview, global, nop, ...) are documented in the exaNBody documentation.

items.title: grid_flavor_mpm
items.text: Selects the exaMPM grid type (MPMFieldSet). Must run before any other grid operator.

items.title: init_nodes
items.text:
Sizes grid_cell_values on the particle grid and adds the MPM nodal fields (mpm_mass, mpm_q, mpm_qdot, mpm_f, mpm_fb). The centre of each cell is one MPM node: the domain must start at -h/2, h being the cell size.

Slot Flow Type Default Description grid_cell_values in/out GridCellValues MPM nodal values, one node per cell

items.title: reset_nodes
items.text:
Sets every nodal value to 0 (discards the previous grid).

Slot Flow Type Default Description grid_cell_values in/out GridCellValues required MPM nodes

items.title: update_mp_cells
items.text:
Lists the cells that hold material points: the MP kernels only loop over these cells.

Slot Flow Type Default Description mp_cells out CellList cells holding MPs

items.title: blender_modify_mp
items.text:
Changes the group and density of the MPs inside the Blender objects (prisms along z), like mpmxdem's blender_modify_MP. As in mpmxdem, the MPs of the lowest and highest z layers are left unchanged. mpmxdem also changes the constitutive model: in exaMPM the model is chosen by group.

Slot Flow Type Default Description group in long required new MP group (selects the constitutive model and contact laws) density in double required new mass density (the mass is updated) file in std::string required 'Object n x y z ...' Blender coordinate file

items.title: blender_set_mp_grid
items.text:
Fills a Blender object with cubic material points of side 'size' (MP centres on a lattice starting at the lower corner of the object bounding box + size/2), at rest and stress free.

Slot Flow Type Default Description group in long 0 MP group, stored in the 'type' field (mpmxdem: groupNb) density in double required mass density file in std::string required Blender geometry file format in std::string "coords" 'coords': 'Object n x y z ...' file of the getCoord script (mpmxdem: blender_set_MP_grid), each object being a prism along z; 'stl': ASCII STL closed mesh (blender_set_MP_grid2) size in double required side of the cubic material points

items.title: move_mp
items.text:
Rotates (Rz * Ry around 'origin') then translates all the MPs, like mpmxdem's move_MP command.

Slot Flow Type Default Description origin in Vec3d [0, 0, 0] centre of the rotations (x0, y0, z0) translation in Vec3d [0, 0, 0] translation applied after the rotation (dx, dy, dz) theta_z in double 0.0 rotation around the z axis (degrees, negative is clockwise) theta_y in double 0.0 rotation around the y axis (degrees)

items.text:
Global MPM parameters shared by the time scheme operators: gravity and mass tolerance.

Slot Flow Type Default Description gravity in/out Vec3d [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] gravity acceleration (mpmxdem: gravity) tolmass in/out double 1.e-6 nodes lighter than this are ignored in grid-to-particle transfers (mpmxdem: tolmass)

items.title: print_simulation_state
items.text:
Prints one log line per call, in the style of exaDEM's print_simulation_state: step, time, number of MPs, active nodes, active MP-obstacle contacts, total mass and volume, average kinetic energy per MP, maximum velocity, mean pressure and the throughput in MP updates per second (MPs x steps / wall-clock seconds since the previous line). The header is printed with the first line.

Slot Flow Type Default Description timestep in long required current time step physical_time in double required current physical time mpm_simulation_state in MPMSimulationState required reduced MPM quantities save_file in bool true also append the log lines to log_file log_file in std::string "ExaMPMOutputDir/log.txt" log file

items.title: save_mp_pos
items.text: Writes the MP positions in /mpPos.txt, one line 'x y z' per MP sorted by id, like mpmxdem's MPMbox::save_MPpos (n = timestep / mpm_vtk_period). Single process only. Slot Flow Type Default Description mp_cells in CellList required cells holding MPs timestep in long required current time step mpm_vtk_period in long 1000 output period, the file index is timestep / period directory in std::string "mpm_mppos" output directory

items.title: set_k0_stress

Geostatic initial stress, like mpmxdem's set_K0_stress command: with d the depth along the gravity below the highest MP, stress.yy = -d g rho0, stress.xx = K0 stress.yy, stress.xy = stress.yx = 0 (the other components are unchanged, as in mpmxdem).

Slot Flow Type Default Description gravity in Vec3d required gravity acceleration nu in double required Poisson ratio used for K0 = nu / (1 - nu) density in double required density of the overburden (mpmxdem: rho0)

items.title: set_mp_grid

Fills a box with cubic material points of side 'size', at rest and stress free, like mpmxdem's set_MP_grid command. Also sets the previous position to the current one (mpmxdem: MPMbox::init).

Slot Flow Type Default Description group in long 0 MP group, stored in the 'type' field (mpmxdem: groupNb) density in double required mass density (mpmxdem: mass_density) lower in Vec3d required lower corner of the box (x0, y0, z0) upper in Vec3d required upper corner of the box (x1, y1, z1) size in double required side of the cubic material points

items.text:
Global MPM quantities for the log (MPs, active nodes, contacts, mass, volume, kinetic energy, max |v|, mean pressure).

items.title: hooke_elasticity

mpmxdem step 4 with the HookeElasticity model: strain increment from q_I/m_I, then linear elastic stress from the total strain.

items.text:
mpmxdem step 3: qdot_I = fb_I + f_I, q_I += qdot_I dt.

Slot Flow Type Default Description grid_cell_values in/out GridCellValues required MPM nodes dt in double required time step

items.text:
mpmxdem: contact forces to the nodes, fb_I += N_I f_p.

Slot Flow Type Default Description mp_cells in CellList required cells holding MPs grid_cell_values in/out GridCellValues required MPM nodes

items.text:

Slot Flow Type Default Description mp_cells in CellList required cells holding MPs grid_cell_values in/out GridCellValues required MPM nodes gravity in Vec3d required gravity

items.title: p2g_mass
items.text:
mpmxdem step 1: m_I += N_I m_p. Aborts if an MP is outside the grid, like mpmxdem.

Slot Flow Type Default Description mp_cells in CellList required cells holding MPs grid_cell_values in/out GridCellValues required MPM nodes

items.title: p2g_momentum
items.text:
mpmxdem step 3b: q_I += N_I m_p v_p.

Slot Flow Type Default Description mp_cells in CellList required cells holding MPs grid_cell_values in/out GridCellValues required MPM nodes

items.title: update_mass
items.text:
mpmxdem step 0: m_p = rho_p V_p.

Slot Flow Type Default Description mp_cells in CellList required cells holding MPs

items.title: update_volume
items.text:
mpmxdem step 4a: volume and density from mp_delta_strain (xx + yy). Mohr-Coulomb does not set it.

Slot Flow Type Default Description mp_cells in CellList required cells holding MPs

items.title: obstacles
items.text:
Creates the rigid obstacles from mpmxdem-style definition lines. As in mpmxdem, the Blender obstacles (Plane2, Sphere2) come after the others. A Cylinder removes the MPs it overlaps, see obstacles_delete_inside.

Slot Flow Type Default Description obstacles in std::vector<std::string> [] one obstacle per line, as mpmxdem's 'Obstacle' and 'blender_Obstacle' commands: 'Sphere group xc yc zc R driveMode ...', 'Plane group x0 y0 z0 x1 y1 z1 x2 y2 z2 x3 y3 z3', 'Cylinder group x y z R length dx dy dz', 'LeftBiplanar group x0 y0 z0 lengthz l1 l2 R angle', 'Plane2 group file' and 'Sphere2 group file driveMode ...' blender_folder in std::string "." folder of the Plane2 / Sphere2 files (mpmxdem: result_folder) legacy_plane in bool false reproduce mpmxdem's Plane / Plane2 bug (tangents and normal not normalized, plane acting on a smaller rectangle). Only for comparisons with mpmxdem mpm_obstacles out MPMObstacles rigid obstacles

items.title: obstacles_correct
items.text:
mpmxdem ModifiedLagrangian, part C: second half velocity update of the free obstacles from the contact force and moment computed by contact_forces.

Slot Flow Type Default Description mpm_obstacles in/out MPMObstacles required rigid obstacles dt in double required time step

items.title: obstacles_delete_inside
items.text:
Removes the MPs overlapping a Cylinder, like mpmxdem's Cylinder::deleteIfInside (run after the MPs and the obstacles are created). As in mpmxdem the test ignores the cylinder length: the MPs closer than R + size/2 to the axis line are removed.

Slot Flow Type Default Description mpm_obstacles in MPMObstacles required rigid obstacles

items.title: obstacles_predict
items.text:
mpmxdem ModifiedLagrangian, part B: moves the obstacles according to their driving mode (velocity Verlet position update and first half velocity update for free obstacles, imposed velocity otherwise).

Slot Flow Type Default Description mpm_obstacles in/out MPMObstacles required rigid obstacles dt in double required time step

items.title: obstacles_reset
items.text:
mpmxdem ModifiedLagrangian, part A: deletes the resultant force and moment of the obstacles and sets their acceleration to gravity.

Slot Flow Type Default Description mpm_obstacles in/out MPMObstacles required rigid obstacles gravity in Vec3d required gravity acceleration

items.title: paraview_obstacles
items.text:
Writes the obstacle surfaces in a legacy VTK polydata file (one file per call), meshed with quads (spheres, cylinder side, LeftBiplanar arc) or one quad per plane. Cell data: obstacle index, group and velocity.

Slot Flow Type Default Description mpm_obstacles in MPMObstacles required rigid obstacles timestep in long required current time step obstacles_vtk_format in std::string "mpm_paraview/obstacles_%09d.vtk" output file name, formatted with the time step sphere_resolution in long 24 number of sectors used to mesh the curved surfaces

items.title: print_obstacles
items.text:
Prints the position, velocity and contact force of the free obstacles.

Slot Flow Type Default Description mpm_obstacles in MPMObstacles required rigid obstacles timestep in long required current time step physical_time in double required current physical time

items.title: check_proximity
items.text:
mpmxdem MPMbox::checkProximity: rebuilding the neighbor lists resets dn (and ft2, except for planes).

Slot Flow Type Default Description mp_cells in CellList required cells holding MPs mpm_obstacles in MPMObstacles required rigid obstacles

items.title: contact_forces
items.text:
mpmxdem MPMbox::boundaryConditions: MP-obstacle contact forces, added to the MP (fx, fy, fz) and, with the opposite sign, to the obstacle.

Slot Flow Type Default Description mp_cells in CellList required cells holding MPs mpm_obstacles in/out MPMObstacles required rigid obstacles mpm_contact_laws in MPMContactLaws required MP-obstacle contact laws dt in double required time step

items.title: contact_laws
items.text:
Defines the MP-obstacle contact parameters per (MP group, obstacle group).

Slot Flow Type Default Description set in std::vector<std::string> [] one parameter per line, same syntax as mpmxdem's 'set' command: ' groupMP groupObst value' mpm_contact_laws out MPMContactLaws MP-obstacle contact laws

items.title: Outputs
items.text: All the outputs are written by mpm_begin_iteration, before the step, at the first step and then periodically.

items.title: Log line
items.text:
mpm_print_log (every mpm_log_period steps) runs simulation_state (global reductions) and print_simulation_state, which prints one line on screen and appends it to ExaMPMOutputDir/log.txt:

     Step     Time               MPs  Act. nodes   Contacts       Mass     Volume    avg. Ec    max |v|    avg. p  Throughput (MP/s)
      100  1.000000e-03         57000        3280       2280  9.120e+02  4.560e-01  6.427e-07  9.810e-03  1.438e+02  4.0420e+06
Column Meaning MPs number of material points Act. nodes nodes heavier than tolmass Contacts material point-obstacle pairs in contact Mass, Volume total mass and volume of the material points avg. Ec average kinetic energy per material point max \|v\| maximum material point velocity avg. p mean pressure \(-\mathrm{tr}(\sigma)/3\) Throughput material point updates per second since the previous line print_simulation_state slot Description Default save_file also write the lines to log_file true log_file log file ExaMPMOutputDir/log.txt

The hook mpm_log_extra runs after the log line. print_obstacles prints the position, velocity and force of each free obstacle:

mpm_log_extra: print_obstacles

obstacle 0 step      100 t 1.000000e-03 pos  3.102000000e+00  1.000097523e+00  1.400000000e+00 vel  2.000000000e+00  9.509500000e-02  0.000000000e+00 force  0.000000000e+00  0.000000000e+00  0.000000000e+00

items.title: ParaView files
items.text:
mpm_vtk_output (every mpm_vtk_period steps) runs mpm_write_paraview by default:

mpm_write_paraview:
  - timestep_file: "mpm_paraview/mpm_%09d"
  - write_paraview:
      binary_mode: true
      write_ghost: false
      write_box: true
      fields: [ "id", "type", "vx", "vy", "vz", "mp_mass", "mp_vol", "mp_stress", "mp_strain" ]
  - paraview_obstacles: { obstacles_vtk_format: "mpm_paraview/obstacles_%09d.vtk" }
  • mpm_paraview/mpm_<step>.pvtp: the material points (VTK XML polydata, compressed binary), with the listed fields, and the domain box;
  • mpm_paraview/obstacles_<step>.vtk: the obstacle surfaces (legacy VTK, ASCII), meshed with quads (spheres, cylinder side and LeftBiplanar arc with sphere_resolution sectors, default 24). Cell data: obstacle index, group and velocity.

To write other fields, override the block, e.g. add "mp_density" or "fx" to fields.

items.title: mpmxdem position files
items.text:
save_mp_pos writes <directory>/mpPos<n>.txt (default mpm_mppos/), one line x y z per material point sorted by id, with n = timestep / mpm_vtk_period, like mpmxdem's save_MPpos. Useful to compare with mpmxdem:

mpm_vtk_output: [ mpm_write_paraview, save_mp_pos ]

items.title: ParaView
items.text:
The output files are made for ParaView (sudo apt install paraview):

  1. File > Open mpm_paraview/mpm_..pvtp (the time series is grouped) and mpm_paraview/obstacles_..vtk;
  2. color the material points by type, mp_mass, mp_vol, or a component of mp_stress / mp_strain (the only fields written);
  3. to see the material points as cubes, apply a Glyph filter (Box, scale mp_vol^(1/3)) or render the points as Point Gaussian.

items.title: Example images
items.text:
The pictures of the tutorials are rendered off screen with pvbatch (ParaView) and the script scripts/render_example.py of this documentation repository:

pvbatch scripts/render_example.py <run dir> <step> <out.png> <MP radius> <color> [azimuth elevation zoom pad]
  • <run dir> holds the mpm_paraview/ folder of a run, <step> is a step with an output (a multiple of mpm_vtk_period). The script stops with the list of available steps when the file does not exist.
  • <MP radius>: half the size of the material points of the deck.
  • <color>: pressure (mean stress \(-\operatorname{tr}\sigma/3\), scale clipped at the 98th percentile), height (y) or type (group 0 beige, group 1 red).
  • The camera looks at the material points (bounds enlarged by pad metres), turned by azimuth and elevation degrees; obstacles are drawn semi-transparent.

The tutorial pictures come from longer runs than the tests, in the build tree:

cd build-exampm/example/piles_one
../exaMPM piles_one.msp --omp_num_threads 4 --set-global-simulation_end_iteration 29999 \
          --set-global-mpm_vtk_period 3000
pvbatch ${DOC_EXAMPM_DIR}/scripts/render_example.py . 27000 piles_one.png 0.07 height 35 25 1.0 0.3
Example Steps run Rendered step MP radius Color Camera (az el zoom pad) sphere_impacting_structure 30000 24000 0.012 pressure 35 25 1.0 0.5 config_a1 10000 (full) 9000 0.006 pressure 0 12 1.0 0.3 sphere_on_slope 30000 27000 0.07 height 35 25 1.0 0.3 slope_two_layers 30000 27000 0.07 type 35 25 1.0 0.3 piles_one 30000 27000 0.07 height 35 25 1.0 0.3

The images are stored as 1200 × 750 PNG in example/<name>/<name>.png (exaMPM) and docs/images/examples/ (this site).

items.title: Blender
items.text:
Blender cannot read VTK files directly. Two ways to render a simulation in Blender:

  • export the data from ParaView (File > Save Data as PLY for the material points, File > Export Scene as glTF for the obstacles) and import it in Blender, then use Geometry Nodes (Instance on Points) to draw the points;
  • or read the .vtp files with a Python script inside Blender (e.g. with meshio) and update the positions at each frame.

Axes

exaMPM's vertical axis is y, Blender's is z: swap y and z when importing.

items.title: Simulation Graph
items.text: The default configuration data/config/main-config.msp defines the simulation block, a fixed sequence of hooks, and the MPM building blocks that MPM decks plug into these hooks.

items.title: Hooks
items.text:
Hook Default Typical MPM deck hw_device_init mpi_comm_world, init_cuda — init_prolog global — input_data nop parameters, domain, grid_flavor_mpm, init_rcb_grid, MP setters, obstacles, contact_laws init_epilog nop mpm_init first_iteration nop — compute_loop nop mpm_compute_loop simulation_epilog nop — hw_device_finalize finalize_cuda —

Extend the application by overriding these hooks (in a deck), never by editing simulation.

items.title: MPM blocks
items.text:
flowchart TD
  loop[mpm_compute_loop] --> begin[mpm_begin_iteration]
  loop --> ml[mpm_modified_lagrangian]
  loop --> next[next_time_step]
  loop --> stop[mpm_compute_loop_stop]
  begin --> vtk[mpm_vtk_if: mpm_vtk_output]
  begin --> log[mpm_log_if: mpm_print_log]
  begin --> prox[mpm_prox_if: check_proximity]
  log --> extra[mpm_log_extra]
  ml --> cm[mpm_constitutive_model]
Block Content Override to... mpm_init init_nodes, update_mp_cells — mpm_compute_loop the time loop, until simulation_end_iteration — mpm_begin_iteration triggers and runs the periodic outputs, log and proximity check — mpm_modified_lagrangian one MPM time step (details) change the scheme mpm_constitutive_model nop required: the constitutive model(s) mpm_vtk_output mpm_write_paraview add save_mp_pos, change the output mpm_write_paraview ParaView files of the MPs and obstacles change the fields written mpm_print_log simulation_state, print_simulation_state, mpm_log_extra — mpm_log_extra nop e.g. print_obstacles

The periods are the global values mpm_vtk_period, mpm_log_period and mpm_prox_period; each output also runs at the first step. The full file is shown in Default YAML.

items.title: main-config.msp
items.text:
# ==========================================
# === exaMPM default configuration       ===
# ==========================================

configuration:
  # default plugins to load
  plugins: []
  logging:
    parallel: false
    debug: false
    profiling: false
  profiling:
    exectime: false
    summary: false
  debug:
    plugins: false
    config: false
    graph: false
    graph_lod: 0
    filter: []
  mpimt: true
  pinethreads: false
  num_threads: {}
  omp_max_nesting: 2

includes:
  - config_globals.msp

print_logo_banner:
  profiling: false
  body:
    - message: |

        ___________ ____  ___    _____      _____    __________     _____
        \_   _____/ \   \/  /   /  _  \    /     \   \______   \   /     \
         |    __)_   \     /   /  /_\  \  /  \ /  \   |     ___/  /  \ /  \
         |        \  /     \  /    |    \ /    Y    \  |    |     /    Y    \
        /_______  / /___/\  \ \____|__  / \____|__  /  |____|     \____|__  /
                \/        \_/         \/          \/                      \/


# ==========================================
# === placeholders (do nothing for now)  ===
# ==========================================
hw_device_init:
  - mpi_comm_world
  - init_cuda

hw_device_finalize:
  - finalize_cuda

init_prolog: global   # default global values: config_globals.msp
input_data: nop
init_epilog: nop
first_iteration: nop
compute_loop: nop
simulation_epilog: nop

# ==========================================
# === MPM building blocks                ===
# ==========================================
# Used by MPM decks, e.g. example/sphere_impacting_structure/sphere_impacting_structure.msp:
#   init_epilog: mpm_init
#   compute_loop: mpm_compute_loop
#   mpm_constitutive_model: [ mohr_coulomb: {...} ]
# Values are given without units and are taken as SI (m, kg, s). Global defaults: config_globals.msp.

mpm_init:
  - init_nodes
  - update_mp_cells

# --- mpmxdem ModifiedLagrangian::advanceOneStep, split into operators ---
mpm_constitutive_model: nop

mpm_modified_lagrangian:
  - update_mp_cells           #    cells holding MPs
  - obstacles_reset       # A) reset obstacle force / moment, acc = gravity
  - zero_particle_force       #    reset MP contact forces
  - reset_nodes           #    discard previous grid
  - obstacles_predict     # B) move the obstacles
  - update_mass           # 0) MP mass
  - p2g_mass              # 1) nodal mass
  - p2g_internal_forces   # 2) internal and gravity nodal forces
  - contact_forces        # 2b) MP-obstacle contacts (boundaryConditions)
  - obstacles_correct     # C) obstacle velocity from contact forces
  - p2g_contact_forces    #    contact forces to the nodes
  - grid_momentum_rate    # 3) qdot = fb + f, q += qdot dt
  - g2p_velocity          # 3a) MP velocity
  - p2g_momentum          # 3b) updated nodal momentum
  - mpm_constitutive_model    # 4) strain and stress
  - update_volume         # 4a) volume and density
  - g2p_position          # 5) MP positions

# --- mpmxdem MPMbox::run: outputs and proximity check before each step ---
mpm_trigger_vtk:
  rebind: { freq: mpm_vtk_period , result: mpm_trigger_vtk }
  body:
    - nth_timestep: { first: true }

mpm_trigger_prox:
  rebind: { freq: mpm_prox_period , result: mpm_trigger_prox }
  body:
    - nth_timestep: { first: true }

mpm_trigger_log:
  rebind: { freq: mpm_log_period , result: mpm_trigger_log }
  body:
    - nth_timestep: { first: true }

mpm_write_paraview:
  - timestep_file: "mpm_paraview/mpm_%09d"
  - write_paraview:
      binary_mode: true
      write_ghost: false
      write_box: true
      fields: [ "id", "type", "vx", "vy", "vz", "mp_mass", "mp_vol", "mp_stress", "mp_strain" ]
  - paraview_obstacles: { obstacles_vtk_format: "mpm_paraview/obstacles_%09d.vtk" }

# optional text output of the MP positions (mpmxdem mpPos<n>.txt), e.g. mpm_vtk_output: [ mpm_write_paraview, save_mp_pos ]
mpm_vtk_output: mpm_write_paraview

mpm_vtk_if:
  condition: mpm_trigger_vtk
  body: [ mpm_vtk_output ]

mpm_prox_if:
  condition: mpm_trigger_prox
  body: [ check_proximity ]

# exaDEM-like log line (simulation_state + print_simulation_state), every mpm_log_period steps.
# Extra outputs at the same period, e.g. mpm_log_extra: print_obstacles
mpm_log_extra: nop

mpm_print_log:
  - simulation_state
  - print_simulation_state: { log_file: "ExaMPMOutputDir/log.txt" }
  - mpm_log_extra

mpm_log_if:
  condition: mpm_trigger_log
  body: [ mpm_print_log ]

mpm_begin_iteration:
  - mpm_trigger_vtk
  - mpm_trigger_prox
  - mpm_trigger_log
  - mpm_vtk_if
  - mpm_log_if
  - mpm_prox_if

mpm_compute_loop_stop:
  profiling: false
  rebind: { end_at: simulation_end_iteration , result: compute_loop_continue }
  body:
    - sim_continue

mpm_compute_loop:
  loop: true
  name: loop
  condition: compute_loop_continue
  body:
    - mpm_begin_iteration
    - mpm_modified_lagrangian
    - next_time_step
    - mpm_compute_loop_stop

# ==========================================
# === simulation program description     ===
# ==========================================
simulation:
  name: sim
  body:
    - print_logo_banner
    - hw_device_init   # provides MPI_COMM_WORLD as a default communicator
    - init_prolog
    - input_data
    - init_epilog
    - first_iteration
    - compute_loop
    - simulation_epilog
    - hw_device_finalize

items.title: config_globals.msp
items.text:
############ some global properties ############
# Default values of the global simulation slots, created by the 'global' operator (run in init_prolog).
# A deck overrides them key by key, e.g. global: { dt: 1.0e-5 , simulation_end_iteration: 49999 }.
# Values are given without units and are taken as SI (m, kg, s).

global:
  dt: 1.0e-5                     # time step (mpmxdem: dt)
  timestep: 0                    # current time step
  physical_time: 0.0             # current time (mpmxdem: t)
  simulation_end_iteration: 0    # last time step: the loop runs timesteps 0 .. simulation_end_iteration
  compute_loop_continue: true
  mpm_vtk_period: 1000           # paraview output period (mpmxdem: vtkPeriod)
  mpm_prox_period: 100           # proximity check period (mpmxdem: proxPeriod)
  mpm_log_period: 1000           # obstacle log period
